name: NPF Åland
summary: Åland Islands association spreading knowledge about neuropsychiatric disabilities and advocating for the rights of people with them, running member support groups and a youth forum called Simuli.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Affiliated with Funktionsrätt Åland and ABF Åland.

name: Albanian Children Foundation
summary: A Tirana-based Albanian charity working on child health broadly, which runs a National Center for Autism and related training and awareness campaigns in Tirana, Farkë, Kukës and Tetova.
notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member, listed under 'Associated Members' as Albania's representative. The organisation's overall remit is broader child-health humanitarian work (also covering thalassemia and general child welfare); autism is one dedicated programme (its National Center for Autism), not its sole focus. Included for country diversity; flagged here for editorial review.

name: AUTEA (Andorra Autism Association)
summary: Andorra's national autism association, based in Andorra la Vella, listed as a full member of Autism-Europe representing autistic people and families in the microstate.
notes: Site returned no readable content to automated fetch (likely a JS-rendered page) despite a live 202 response; existence and details drawn from Autism-Europe's official August 2026 member directory. Founding year and leadership composition unconfirmed.

name: DISFAM Argentina
summary: The Argentine chapter of the international DISFAM dyslexia network, raising awareness of dyslexia and other learning disabilities and pushing schools and education ministries toward detection and support protocols since 2013.
notes: Founded by parents, teachers and health professionals; part of the Spain-headquartered international DISFAM network, not an independent Argentine organization.

name: Frente de Artistas del Borda
summary: Arts collective founded in 1984 inside Buenos Aires' Borda psychiatric hospital, made up of current and former patients working alongside community members and professionals across theatre, music, and visual-arts workshops.
notes: Blog itself dormant since ~2012, but org's continued activity confirmed via 40th-anniversary (2024) press coverage and a live YouTube channel. A commonly cited domain, frentedeartistasdelbord.com, does not resolve (dead).

name: FUBIPA (Argentine Bipolar Foundation)
name_local: Fundación Bipolares de la República Argentina
summary: A Buenos Aires mutual-aid foundation for people with bipolar disorder and their families, running free peer support groups since 1989 alongside professional-led psychoeducation workshops.
notes: Founded by two psychiatrists, two people with bipolar disorder, and a family member; describes itself as the oldest volunteer association for serious mental disorders in Latin America. Peer-run mutual-aid groups; governing council traditionally chaired by a professional.

name: Mad in Argentina
summary: An editorial platform on mad culture, mental health and neurodiversity in Argentina, part of the international Mad in the World network, publishing essays and interviews from activists, journalists and a national disability-agency staffer.
notes: Team includes a self-described Latin American mad-movement activist alongside journalists; actively publishing as of September 2026.

name: Mad Pride Buenos Aires (Orgullo Loco)
summary: A Buenos Aires platform of mutual support and activism run by neurodivergent and psychiatric-survivor people, organizing around Mad Pride to contest psychiatric stigma, pathologization and institutionalization.
notes: Self-describes as a platform of association and mutual support formed by neurodivergent people; corroborated by Pikara Magazine and academic literature on the Latin American Orgullo Loco movement. Facebook is its only confirmed public presence.

name: PANAACEA
name_local: Programa Argentino para Niños, Adolescentes y Adultos con Condiciones del Espectro Autista
summary: Argentine multi-site research programme studying autism prevalence, early detection and services across the country, coordinating clinicians and researchers with public health institutions.

name: ADHD Foundation Australia
summary: Community-funded, volunteer-run national Australian charity based in Epping, NSW, providing ADHD counselling, screening, group therapy and a helpline for more than 14,000 people and families a year.
notes: Distinct from the UK's Liverpool-based ADHD Foundation, which shares the generic name.

name: Amaze
summary: Victoria's peak autism body, providing information, advocacy, and support for autistic people and their families.
notes: Board includes at least one autistic member alongside parents of autistic adults; not stated as autistic-led.

name: Arts Project Australia
summary: Arts Project Australia is a Melbourne studio and gallery founded in 1974 by Myra Hilgendorf, the first full-time art studio in Australia dedicated to artists with intellectual disability, now supporting more than 150 artists.
notes: Site's own tagline calls itself an organisation 'championing neurodivergent artists and artists with intellectual disability.'

name: Aspect Research Centre for Autism Practice
summary: Research arm of Autism Spectrum Australia (Aspect) that studies autism education and practice and works to translate findings into classroom and service delivery methods.

name: Australian Dyslexia Association (ADA)
summary: Non-profit Australian body concerned with identification, education and structured-literacy instruction for people with dyslexia, offering screening, teacher accreditation and a directory of qualified professionals.
region: Australia (national, no fixed HQ city stated)
notes: Incorporated association (IA37281) and Global Network Partner of the International Dyslexia Association; no single headquarters city stated on site.

name: auticon Australia
summary: Australian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: Autism Advisory & Support Service (AASS)
summary: Liverpool, NSW social enterprise and NDIS provider offering therapy, carer support groups, employment pathways and community advocacy for autistic children and adults.

name: Autism Association of Australia
summary: Sydney national body, founded in 2007 as Autism Awareness Australia and rebranded in 2026, providing age-stage guidance, educator training and community resources for autistic Australians and families.
notes: Rebranded from Autism Awareness Australia to Autism Association of Australia in 2026; CEO Nicole Rogerson.

name: Autism CRC (Cooperative Research Centre for Living with Autism)
summary: University of Queensland-based Australian research centre, established in 2013, co-funding participatory autism research and programmes such as the DXC Dandelion employment programme.
notes: Academic-run, not self-advocate-led.

name: Autistic Self Advocacy Network Australia and New Zealand (ASAN AUNZ)
summary: Grassroots autistic-led advocacy network doing systemic advocacy and self-advocacy skill-building across Australia and New Zealand.
notes: Binational (Australia and New Zealand); member of the Australian Autism Alliance; organisationally distinct from ASAN in the USA.

name: Back to Back Theatre
summary: Contemporary theatre company in Geelong whose ensemble consists of actors with disability; founded 1987, led by non-disabled Artistic Director Bruce Gladwin with a full-time disabled ensemble at its creative core.
notes: Ensemble members are neurodivergent/disabled; Artistic Director Bruce Gladwin is not disclosed as disabled. No 'led by disabled people' claim found on site.

name: DXC Dandelion Program
summary: Corporate autism employment initiative run by DXC Technology since 2014, in partnership with universities and Autism CRC, with 17 teams and over 250 autistic employees across Australia.
notes: Reports 92% retention rate among autistic employees; a corporate CSR programme, not autistic-led.

name: I CAN Network
summary: Autistic-led group mentoring organisation delivering school-based and online mentoring programmes for autistic and neurodivergent young people in Australia and New Zealand.
notes: Founder is autistic; reports 77% of staff are autistic and requires a minimum of half; reaches both Australia and New Zealand.

name: Rawcus
summary: Melbourne ensemble theatre company creating devised performance work with an ensemble of performers with and without disability.
notes: Originated via a partnership between Theatreworks, disability organisation Scope, and the City of Port Phillip. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent.

name: Reframing Autism
summary: Australian registered charity providing education, resources, courses, and advocacy on autism, run by and for autistic people.
notes: Operates nationally with no single fixed HQ city stated; registered with the ACNC.

name: Restless Dance Theatre
summary: Adelaide-based inclusive contemporary dance company founded in 1991 by Sally Chance and Tania Rose, building careers for disabled and neurodivergent dancers.
notes: Founded by non-disabled artists. Company's own history notes a former artistic director (2009) was 'the first artistic director with a disability in any Australian dance company', and current AD Michelle Ryan (since 2013) has MS — but no blanket 'disability-led' institutional claim, so kept as mixed.

name: SPELD Queensland
summary: Queensland not-for-profit, operating for over 50 years in partnership with Education Queensland, providing psychoeducational and ADHD assessment, tutoring and teacher training for people with specific learning difficulties.
notes: A Queensland state body, distinct from national or other state SPELD federations.

name: Studio A
summary: Studio A is a supported studio based in St Leonards, Sydney, led by CEO/Artistic Director Gabrielle Mordy, providing professional development and commercial representation to artists with intellectual disability.
notes: Founding year not stated on the mission/impact pages checked; could not verify this session.

name: Tourette's Australia
summary: Australian support and advocacy organisation for people with Tourette syndrome and tic disorders, publishing school and parent resources and research such as the IMPACT tic-disorder study.
region: Australia (national, no fixed HQ city stated)
notes: Headquarters city not stated on site.

name: Yellow Ladybugs
summary: Autistic-led Australian organisation running community events, education, and advocacy for autistic girls, women, and gender-diverse people.
notes: CEO/founder is autistic; site states it is 'proudly autistic-led and neuro affirming'.

name: Austrian Autism Aid (ÖAH)
summary: A Vienna-based nonprofit that grew out of a parents' self-help group into Austria's federal coordination centre for autism, offering free family counselling, diagnostics, therapy, job coaching, and specialist training.
notes: Not an Autism-Europe member as of the August 2026 directory (Austria has no listed AE member); found independently as Austria's national coordination and advocacy body. Explicitly emerged from a parent self-help group. Founding year not stated on the site.

name: Austrian Federal Association for Dyslexia (ÖBVL)
summary: Austrian dyslexia association providing certified training for dyslexia therapists, professional continuing education, therapist directories and public information on dyslexia.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Headquarters city not stated on the site; Vienna used as a national placeholder.

name: Intervoice Oberoesterreich
summary: An Austrian peer-led hearing-voices network based in Linz, operating within the psychosocial association EXIT-sozial, running monthly self-help groups, phone counselling and the annual World Hearing Voices Day.
notes: Founding year approximate: a 2018 page referenced 'almost 25 years' of activity, implying roughly 1993-1994. Involves peer 'experience experts' in leadership roles alongside professional supporters at EXIT-sozial.

name: Museum Gugging
summary: Art brut complex in Maria Gugging (Klosterneuburg) built around the Haus der Künstler, a residence-studio for artists with psychiatric/intellectual disabilities opened 1981 under psychiatrist Leo Navratil; the museum building dates to 2006.
notes: Museum itself operated by NÖ Museum Betriebs GmbH under artistic director Johann Feilacher (psychiatrist), not by the resident artists. The adjacent galerie gugging (separate site, galeriegugging.com) is owned by the Gugging Artists collective — worth a separate look if a more nd-led entry is wanted.

name: Autism BD
summary: Bangladeshi informational portal on autism and neurodevelopmental disorders, developed under the Bangladesh Society of NeuroDevelopment & Research Trust with input from neuro-rehabilitation professionals.
notes: An information and directory hub for families rather than a direct-service provider; site explicitly disclaims being a treatment resource.

name: Shuchona Foundation
summary: Dhaka foundation, founded in 2014 as an evolution of an earlier Global Autism initiative, working on autism and neurodevelopmental-disability policy, awareness and a mobile screening app.
notes: Founded and chaired by Saima Wazed, daughter of a former Bangladeshi prime minister and a senior WHO regional official; site returns 403 to automated bot checks, existence confirmed via Wikipedia.

name: The Society for the Welfare of Autistic Children (SWAC)
summary: Dhaka-based nonprofit founded in 2000 by parents of autistic individuals, running a school, therapy services, respite care, and a social enterprise for people with autism.
notes: Executive Committee is mainly composed of parents of autistic individuals.

name: Autisme Centraal
summary: Flemish training and resource centre in Belgium that educates teachers, care staff and families on autism and publishes practical guidance for schools and workplaces.

name: Collectif Autiste de Belgique
summary: A peer-support collective created by and for autistic adults, or those questioning their neurotype, in French-speaking Belgium, offering meetings and mutual aid to fill gaps in adult autism support.
notes: Founding year not stated on the site. Listed in the Maison de l'Autisme Brussels directory alongside other Belgian autism organisations.

name: Dr. Guislain Museum
summary: Museum of the history of psychiatry and outsider art, housed in Belgium's oldest psychiatric hospital (inaugurated 1857) in Ghent, founded on the reform work of Dr. Joseph Guislain.
notes: Exact year the museum (as opposed to the 1857 hospital) opened to the public could not be confirmed from primary sources; secondary sources vary (1980s). Run by the Guislain psychiatric institution/foundation, not by patients or an nd-led body.

name: Kunsthuis Yellow Art
summary: An art studio in Geel, Belgium for people with psychiatric or mental-health vulnerabilities, established as a permanent facility in 2004 by OPZ Geel, a public psychiatric care center; professional artists collaborate with about 30 participants outside a therapeutic framework.
notes: Linked to OPZ Geel (public psychiatric hospital); grew out of the 2001 'Y.E.L.L.O.W.' exhibition curated by Jan Hoet. Serves psychiatric patients broadly, not a disability-specific studio.

name: La "S" Grand Atelier
summary: A center for art brut and contemporary art in Vielsalm, Belgium, founded in 1992 by director Anne-Francoise Rouche as a creative workshop for artists with intellectual disabilities, which also hosts professional artists for co-creation residencies.
notes: Official site is live (HTTP 200) but currently shows only an 'under reconstruction' placeholder — facts sourced from BPS22's exhibition page and the Vielsalm tourism site instead. Recognized as a Centre d'Art Brut & Contemporain by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation in 2019.

name: LAVA (Reading and Advisory Group of Adults with Autism)
name_local: Lees- en Adviesgroep Volwassenen met Autisme
summary: Ghent-based Flemish group of autistic adults that critically reviews autism research, advises on research priorities and media framing, and organises public lectures and reading salons on autism from a neurodiversity perspective.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. States 'we are adults with autism'; partners with Leuven Autism Research and the Flemish Autism Action Plan.

name: REV Belgium (Hearing Voices Network Belgium)
name_local: Réseau sur l'Entente de Voix Belgique
summary: French-speaking Belgian node of the international Hearing Voices Network, listed by Intervoice as the national contact for hearing-voices peer support in Belgium.
notes: Listed on Intervoice's national-networks directory.

name: TAKTO (formerly Passwerk)
summary: Belgian IT consultancy employing autistic professionals as software testers and consultants, rebranded from Passwerk to TAKTO while keeping its autism-employment model.
notes: passwerk.be now redirects to takto.be.

name: Balkan Voices Network
summary: A regional Hearing Voices network coordinating national representatives in Bosnia and Herzegovina (Tavan), Croatia (Dom Turnić), Serbia (Prostor) and Slovenia, running peer 'Art of Voices' training and an Erasmus+ Balkan Recovery College.
region: Sarajevo (regional network spanning four countries; host city not stated)
notes: Country field is an approximation: the network lists a Bosnian member (Tavan) first, but coordinates activity across Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia and Slovenia. Affiliated with Intervoice.

name: AAMPARA (AMA Curitiba)
name_local: Associação de Atendimento e Apoio ao Autista do Brasil (AAMPARA), trade name AMA - Amigos Pelo Autista
summary: Curitiba nonprofit founded in 2006 to improve the quality of life of autistic children and adolescents, operating under the trade name AMA within the national AMA network.

name: ABDA - Brazilian Attention Deficit Association
name_local: Associação Brasileira do Déficit de Atenção (ABDA)
summary: National patient association for ADHD, founded in Rio de Janeiro in 1999 and affiliated with the ADHD World Federation. Runs free monthly support groups in eight cities, trains health and education professionals, and helped shape Brazil's 2021 federal law on student health and education rights.
region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
notes: Official domain tdah.org.br did not respond during verification (connection timeout from this network, DNS resolves fine); existence and current activity confirmed via its active YouTube channel and USP-hosted institutional materials referencing it.

name: ABRACA - Brazilian Association for Action for the Rights of Autistic People
name_local: Associação Brasileira para Ação por Direitos das Pessoas Autistas (ABRAÇA)
summary: A national rights organization for autistic people, based in Fortaleza, Ceará. States it is led by autistic people and allied human-rights defenders, and works on self-advocacy, deinstitutionalization, and legal protections grounded in neurodiversity and the CRPD.
notes: Founding year (2008) drawn from secondary coverage, not stated on the current site. Explicitly describes itself as 'protagonizada e liderada por pessoas autistas' (protagonized and led by autistic people).

name: Acessa BH Festival
summary: Belo Horizonte's annual disability-culture arts festival, in its sixth edition in 2026, curated by disabled curators Daniel and Lais Vitral under the principle 'nothing about us without us.' Programs dance, theatre, film, and literature across six venues, including neurodivergent artists.
notes: Founding year inferred from '6th edition' in 2026, not directly confirmed. A broader disability-culture festival (physical, sensory, intellectual, and neurodivergent artists), not exclusively a neurodiversity event; included for its explicit disability-led curation model.

name: Acre State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado do Acre (FEAPAES-AC)
summary: Rio Branco-based state federation supporting local APAE chapters across Acre, including smaller-city affiliates such as Sena Madureira, and campaigning on disability rights.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: AMA - Association of Friends of the Autistic (São Paulo)
summary: Founded in São Paulo in 1983 by parents of autistic children, the first autism association in Brazil and Latin America. Runs education, therapy and social-assistance programmes and maintains a national directory of partner autism institutions.
notes: Won the UNESCO Human Rights Prize in 1998. Anchor organisation of a nationwide network of independently run AMA-branded associations in other cities and states, several catalogued separately in this file.

name: AMA Alagoas
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Alagoas
summary: Parent-founded autism association in Maceió, part of the national AMA network, providing therapy, education and family support for autistic children and adults in Alagoas state.
notes: Listed as AMA-AL in AMA São Paulo's national institution directory.

name: AMA Amazonas (Manaus)
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista do Amazonas
summary: Manaus autism association founded in 1997 by parents and friends of autistic people, the only organisation in the city serving autistic adults from age 14, offering social-assistance, health and education services.
notes: No independent working website found (only social media); existence and current activity confirmed via a Manaus municipal government news article about a service partnership.

name: AMA Campo Grande
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Campo Grande
summary: Mato Grosso do Sul autism association in the national AMA network, providing therapy, special education and family support services in Campo Grande.
region: Campo Grande, Mato Grosso do Sul
notes: Listed as AMA-MS in AMA São Paulo's national institution directory.

name: AMA Florianópolis
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Florianópolis
summary: Santa Catarina autism association affiliated with the national AMA network, providing education, therapeutic support and family guidance for autistic people in Florianópolis.
notes: Listed as AMA-SC Florianópolis in AMA São Paulo's national institution directory.

name: AMA Itajaí
summary: Autism association in Itajaí, Santa Catarina, describing its mission as building a society where autistic people 'have a place and a voice,' offering therapeutic and educational support.

name: AMA Joinville
name_local: Associação dos Amigos do Autista de Joinville
summary: Santa Catarina autism association serving Joinville and the surrounding region with therapeutic, educational and family-support services, part of the national AMA network.

name: AMA Ribeirão Preto
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista de Ribeirão Preto
summary: Family-founded autism association in Ribeirão Preto, São Paulo state, offering education, therapeutic care and support groups for autistic people and their relatives.
notes: Independent AMA-network affiliate, distinct from the USP Ribeirão Preto Hearing Voices Network already catalogued in this city.

name: AMAES - Friends of Autistic People of Espírito Santo
name_local: Associação de Amigos do Autista do Espírito Santo (AMAES)
summary: State-wide autism association founded in 2001 and headquartered in Vitória, with units across Espírito Santo, offering social assistance, specialised education, health and rehabilitation services and public-awareness campaigns.
notes: Operates additional units in Aracruz, Serra, Cariacica, Vila Velha and Viana.

name: AMAI - Friends of Autistic People of Itu
name_local: AMAI - Associação Amigos dos Autistas de Itu
summary: Family-founded association in Itu, São Paulo state, providing therapeutic, educational and social-assistance support to autistic children, youth and adults.
notes: Part of the wider network of AMA-branded family associations in São Paulo state municipalities.

name: AMAS - Friends of Autistic People of Sorocaba
name_local: Associação Amigos dos Autistas de Sorocaba (AMAS)
summary: Nonprofit founded in Sorocaba, São Paulo state, in 1994 for the diagnosis, treatment and habilitation of autistic children aged 2 to 12, with health, education and social-assistance services and family support.
notes: Part of the AMA-affiliated network of family-founded autism associations across Brazil, independently incorporated in Sorocaba.

name: APAE Aracaju
summary: Sergipe chapter of the APAE network, founded in 1970, serving around 600 people with intellectual and multiple disabilities across 33 municipalities and running an explicit self-advocacy (autodefensoria) programme.
notes: Site explicitly names an Autodefensoria strengthening self-advocates' protagonism, so marked mixed leadership rather than purely ally-led.

name: APAE Belo Horizonte
summary: Belo Horizonte chapter of the APAE network, operating for more than 60 years, running a health clinic, an inclusive school, supported-employment programmes and residential care for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: No self-advocacy programme found stated on its site, unlike APAE Aracaju or APAE Três Pontas catalogued separately.

name: APAE Florianópolis
summary: Florianópolis chapter of the APAE network, providing services for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities in Santa Catarina's capital.
notes: Site content was minimal at verification time; included for state/city coverage as a working, live local APAE chapter distinct from the autism-specific AMA Florianópolis catalogued separately.

name: APAE Três Pontas
summary: Local chapter of the APAE network in Três Pontas, Minas Gerais, serving about 4,000 people with intellectual and other disabilities through education, rehabilitation, supported employment and a dedicated Self-Management, Self-Advocacy and Family Program.
notes: Included as an example of a local APAE chapter with an explicit self-advocacy (autogestão/autodefesa) programme, distinct from the national and state federations catalogued separately.

name: ASTOC - Solidarity Association for OCD and Tourette Syndrome
name_local: Astoc ST - Associação Solidária do TOC e Síndrome de Tourette
summary: São Paulo association founded in 1996 to spread information on OCD and Tourette syndrome, fund research and support patient socialisation, running peer support groups with trained facilitators and partner groups in other states.
notes: Partners with RIOSTOC (Rio de Janeiro, already catalogued) and with hospital-based OCD programme PROTOC, also catalogued in this file.

name: AUMA - Friends of the Autistic Child Association
name_local: AUMA - Associação dos Amigos da Criança Autista
summary: São Paulo association providing clinical, psychoeducational and psychomotor support for autistic children and adults, staffed by social workers, psychomotor therapists and pedagogical specialists.
notes: Distinct from same-acronym AMA-network entities in other states; based in São Paulo city, not to be confused with any Rio Grande do Sul organisation of a similar name.

name: Autism and Reality
summary: São Paulo organisation founded in 2010 by parents after their daughter's autism diagnosis, publishing guidance booklets and research since 2015 under the José Luiz Egydio Setúbal Foundation's PENSI Institute, combining a parents' council with a professional council.
notes: Also awards the A&R Prof. Dr. Marcos Tomanik Mercadante prize for autism research and training.

name: Autistic Collective of UFPB
summary: Student-run collective at the Federal University of Paraíba in João Pessoa supporting autistic students, seeking volunteer professionals to assist members and running accessibility workshops such as AI-for-accessibility sessions.
notes: Part of the wave of autistic student collectives that followed USP's CAUSP (already catalogued) from 2021 onward.

name: Autistic Collective of UFRGS
summary: Student collective at the Federal University of Rio Grande do Sul in Porto Alegre, founded in 2021 as part of the wave of autistic collectives inspired by USP's CAUSP. Provides a welcoming space and mutual support for autistic students, including those admitted through disability quotas.
region: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul
notes: No independent website found; verified via UFRGS's own newspaper. Part of the CAUSP-inspired network of university autistic collectives; exact internal leadership composition not independently confirmed.

name: Autistic Collective of USP (CAUSP)
summary: Student collective at the University of São Paulo, founded in 2021 by an autistic undergraduate to support autistic students' retention in higher education. Runs peer mentoring, support groups, and awareness campaigns; inspired similar collectives at over 20 other Brazilian universities.
notes: No independent website; operates via Instagram/Facebook (@coletivoautista). Founder Giulia Jardim Martinovic is autistic; collective won 2nd place in USP's 2021 Diversity Prize.

name: Autistic Collective of Vitória da Conquista
name_local: Coletivo Autista de Vitória da Conquista
summary: University collective formed in 2022 by autistic students from UESB, IFBA, UFBA and private colleges in Vitória da Conquista, Bahia, meeting biweekly to build visibility and mutual support around neurodivergence in higher education.
notes: No independent website found; verified via local news outlet. Multi-institution collective spanning one public state university, one federal institute and one federal university.

name: Brazilian Autism Pride Movement (MOAB)
summary: Founded in Brasília in 2005 by relatives of autistic people, one of Brazil's oldest national autism organizations. Runs the annual June 18 Autism Pride Day campaign and lobbies Congress on autism policy; family-led rather than a self-advocacy group.
notes: Official domain moab.org.br no longer resolves; verified via Wikipedia, an active Instagram/Facebook presence (@moabbrasil), and Brazilian Congress recognition of its 10th anniversary.

name: Brazilian Dyslexia Association (ABD)
summary: Founded in São Paulo in 1983 by the father of a child with dyslexia. Offers technical guidance to dyslexic people, families, and educators, and lobbies for legislation and workplace access; one of Brazil's oldest learning-disability organizations.

name: Brazilian Federation of Down Syndrome Associations
name_local: Federação Brasileira das Associações de Síndrome de Down (FBASD)
summary: Brasília-based federation, founded in 1994, uniting more than 50 Down syndrome associations across Brazil's five regions; created a National Group of Self-Advocates in 2016 that trains young people and adults with Down syndrome as self-advocates and mediators.
notes: Federation itself is run by member associations and professionals, but explicitly sponsors a national self-advocates group of people with Down syndrome.

name: Campinas Hearing Voices Group (CEI)
name_local: CEI Campinas - Grupo de Ouvidores de Vozes
summary: Peer support group for voice-hearers run by the Centro de Estudos e Pesquisas em Reabilitação (CEI) in Campinas, part of the Brazilian offshoot of the international Hearing Voices Movement.
notes: Sister initiative to the USP Ribeirão Preto Hearing Voices Network already catalogued in this dataset; part of a wider set of Brazilian Ouvidores de Vozes groups that also met in Curitiba, Belo Horizonte and Porto Alegre without independent websites found.

name: Canal Autismo / Revista Autismo
summary: Brazilian autism media outlet publishing Revista Autismo, launched in 2010 as the first Portuguese-language autism magazine, by the nonprofit Consciência Solidária based in Atibaia, São Paulo; distributes news, a free quarterly print edition and video content.
notes: Site blocks bare automated requests (403) but was confirmed live via search-engine indexing and third-party citation; described as the first magazine on autism in Latin America and the world.

name: Casa da Esperança Foundation
summary: Fortaleza-based foundation providing autism diagnosis, education and family-training services, an early producer of Brazilian podcasts on autism and a long-running reference institution in Ceará.
notes: Site only resolves over plain HTTP, not HTTPS, in verification checks; distinct from ABRAÇA, also based in Fortaleza.

name: Centro Conviver
summary: Curitiba clinical and educational centre founded in 1998 serving autistic adolescents, young adults and adults using the TEACCH model, working with families, schools, universities and employers on inclusion.
notes: One of the few Brazilian autism organisations focused specifically on adolescents and adults rather than young children.

name: Cia. Teatral Ueinzz
summary: Theatre company in São Paulo, founded around 1997, whose ensemble mixes users of mental health/psychiatric services with professional actors and philosophers, closely associated with philosopher Peter Pál Pelbart.
notes: No dedicated official website found; sources vary on exact founding year (1996-1999). Confirmed active via a May 2024 performance listing. Peter Pál Pelbart is named as an actor-coordinator/member, not simply an outside academic observer. (original url https://x.com/ueinzz was a social-media link; replaced with source page)

name: Hearing Voices Network - USP Ribeirão Preto
summary: Hearing-voices peer information network based at the University of São Paulo's Ribeirão Preto campus, built jointly by voice-hearers and researchers at the Laboratory of Teaching and Research in Psychopathology, Drugs and Society. Shares coping strategies and hosts an in-person support group.
notes: Founding year not stated. Site describes itself as built collaboratively by lived-experience voice-hearers and professional researchers, part of the international Hearing Voices Movement/Intervoice framework.

name: Instituto ABCD
summary: Nonprofit founded in São Paulo in 2009 by a family member of a person with dyslexia. Develops the free EduEdu learning app used by over a million students, trains teachers through its 'Todos Aprendem' program, and advocates for policy on dyslexia and other learning disorders.

name: Instituto Lagarta Vira Pupa
summary: Online support network for families of disabled and autistic people, grown from a 2012 blog by journalist Andréa Werner after her son's autism diagnosis into an institute in 2021 with around 300 volunteer ambassadors nationwide.
notes: Parent-led rather than autistic-led. No single fixed office confirmed; site content references São Paulo, Bauru and Campinas, so the São Paulo coordinate is an approximation for a nationwide online network.

name: Introvertendo
summary: Podcast and media outlet founded in Goiânia in 2018 by autistic students from the Federal University of Goiás, billed as Brazil's first podcast produced by autistic people. Paused in 2023 and relaunched in 2025 under production by NAIA Autismo with new hosts.
notes: Site reachable (301 redirect to www subdomain, then 200). At least 80% of original-run guests were autistic; site includes audio description and Libras support.

name: LEPED – Laboratory for Studies and Research in Education and Difference, UNICAMP
name_local: Laboratório de Estudos e Pesquisas em Ensino e Diferença
summary: Research lab at the University of Campinas studying inclusive education for disabled and neurodivergent students, training teachers, and publishing on school inclusion policy in Brazil.

name: Mad in Brasil
summary: Brazilian outlet of the international Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, lived-experience narratives, and mad-studies scholarship. Hosted at Fiocruz's National School of Public Health (ENSP) in Rio de Janeiro and runs a virtual library on psychiatric medication.
region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
notes: Founding year not confirmed. Editorial leadership not disclosed in detail; publishes both academic/professional content and first-person accounts from psychiatric survivors.

name: Mato Grosso State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado de Mato Grosso (FEAPAES-MT)
summary: Cuiabá-based state federation linking local APAE associations across Mato Grosso, running training programmes and self-advocacy and self-management forums for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: Site describes forums for self-advocacy and self-management (autogestão), so marked mixed rather than purely ally-led. State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately.

name: Museum of Images of the Unconscious
summary: Rio de Janeiro museum founded in 1952 by psychiatrist Nise da Silveira within a former psychiatric hospital in Engenho de Dentro, housing roughly 350,000 artworks made by psychiatric patients through occupational art therapy.
region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
notes: Collection registered as Brazilian national heritage by IPHAN; part of the Instituto Municipal Nise da Silveira, whose grounds also host the Loucura Suburbana carnival bloc catalogued separately.

name: National Anti-Asylum Struggle Movement (MNLA)
summary: National psychiatric-reform movement consolidated in 1993 at its first national meeting in Salvador, bringing together psychiatric-service users, family members, and mental-health workers. Campaigns against asylum-based care and organized May 18 as Brazil's National Anti-Asylum Struggle Day.
notes: National movement with no fixed headquarters or independent website; located at the city of its founding national meeting (Salvador, 1993). Has an active Facebook page (mnlaemluta) that could not be verified via automated request from this network. Explicitly composed of 'usuários, familiares e trabalhadores' (users, family members, and workers).

name: National Federation of APAEs
summary: Brasília-based umbrella federation of more than 2,000 local APAE associations serving people with intellectual and multiple disabilities across Brazil, operating for over 60 years and running a national self-advocates programme (Encontro Nacional de Autodefensores).
notes: Historically family- and professional-led, but its self-advocacy programme has produced autodefensores who represent users on bodies such as the National Social Assistance Council. Several state federations (FEAPAES) are catalogued separately in this file.

name: Pernambuco State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação Estadual das APAEs de Pernambuco (FEAPAES-PE)
summary: State federation coordinating APAE chapters across Pernambuco, headquartered in Caruaru, providing training and resource support to affiliated associations serving people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: PROTOC - Obsessive-Compulsive Spectrum Disorders Program
summary: Research, teaching and patient-care programme on the obsessive-compulsive spectrum run by the Psychiatry Institute of the University of São Paulo's Hospital das Clínicas, recruiting research volunteers and publishing patient-facing education.
notes: Hospital- and university-affiliated, not self-advocate led. Listed as a partner organisation by ASTOC, catalogued separately.

name: Rio Grande do Norte State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado do Rio Grande do Norte (FEAPAES-RN)
summary: Natal-based state federation coordinating APAE chapters across Rio Grande do Norte, providing educational programmes, social services and community-inclusion initiatives for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: RIOSTOC
name_local: Riostoc - Associação de familiares, amigos e pessoas com TOC e Síndrome de Tourette
summary: Rio de Janeiro support association for people with OCD and Tourette syndrome and their families, coordinated by volunteer family members with input from mental-health professionals at UFRJ's IPUB and DPA. Holds free monthly online meetings and shares coping information.
region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
notes: Founding year not stated on site. Explicitly coordinated by volunteer family members, advised by volunteer psychiatrists/psychologists; directs members to public healthcare rather than private practice.

name: Specialisterne Brasil
summary: São Paulo branch of the international Specialisterne network for autistic and neurodivergent employment. Trains autistic and neurodivergent jobseekers and places them with corporate clients including Itaú, IBM, and Carrefour, while advising companies on inclusive hiring and diversity training.
notes: Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the Brazilian site; part of the international Specialisterne network founded in Denmark in 2004.

name: Stim Collective (UFPR)
summary: Autistic student collective at the Federal University of Paraná in Curitiba, launched as a university extension project to build representation and peer support for autistic students on campus.
notes: No independent website found; UFPR's accessibility coordination (CAS) separately reports serving 677 autistic students as of the source article.

name: Suburban Madness Carnival Bloc
summary: Rio de Janeiro carnival bloc and cultural centre created in 2001 at the Instituto Municipal Nise da Silveira, bringing mental-health service users, family members, staff and neighbours together for street carnival and, since 2010, year-round workshops in samba, music and costume-making.
region: Rio de Janeiro, Rio de Janeiro
notes: Rio's first mental-health Ponto de Cultura (Culture Point), 2010. Located on the same grounds as the Museum of Images of the Unconscious, catalogued separately.

name: Tocantins State Federation of APAEs
name_local: Federação das APAEs do Estado do Tocantins (FEAPAES-TO)
summary: Palmas-based state federation coordinating APAE chapters across Tocantins, facilitating educational programmes, employment opportunities and cultural events for people with intellectual and multiple disabilities.
notes: State-level affiliate of Federação Nacional das APAEs, catalogued separately in this file.

name: UFPA Accessibility Coordination
summary: Accessibility unit of the Federal University of Pará in Belém providing individualised pedagogical, psychological and occupational-therapy support to autistic and intellectually disabled students, alongside Libras and Braille services for other disabilities.
notes: Institutional support unit, not a student-run collective; reports serving 20 autistic and 8 intellectually disabled students as of the source article. No specific Indigenous or quilombola programme found despite searching.

name: UFSC Neurodivergent Students Project
name_local: Neurodivergentes: vivências de estudantes autistas no ensino superior (UFSC)
summary: University extension project at the Federal University of Santa Catarina in Florianópolis, coordinated by education professor Wellington Oliveira dos Santos. Runs recurring online sessions where autistic students and community members discuss higher-education experiences, employment, and identity.
notes: Run as a recurring extension course (fourth edition as of February 2026); exact founding year and whether facilitators are themselves autistic are not stated in the source.

name: UFU Autism Spectrum Collective
name_local: Coletivo de estudantes com TEA da UFU
summary: Student collective at the Federal University of Uberlândia founded in April 2023, proposed by an autistic journalism student and supported by two professors, meeting regularly and communicating through Instagram.
notes: Proposed by autistic student Paulo Félix with staff backing from professors Valéria Asnis and Nuno Manna; no independent website, only Instagram.

name: UnB Autism and Neurodiversity Nucleus
name_local: Núcleo de Autismo e Neurodiversidade da UnB
summary: Support nucleus at the University of Brasília created jointly by autistic and neurodivergent students and psychology staff, offering psychological care, guidance for professors and an annual Autism Visibility Week.
notes: Source article quotes autistic and neurodivergent students describing the nucleus as their own initiative, run jointly with psychology-service staff; linked to UnB's Center for Psychological Care and Studies (Caep).

name: Autism Today Association
summary: A Bulgarian nonprofit founded in 2015, running four applied-behaviour-analysis therapy centres in Sofia, Pleven and Burgas for over 1,000 children a year, alongside training and policy-advocacy campaigns.
notes: Established by ABA specialists, community members and parents. Primary activity is clinical ABA therapy delivery, which sits close to the ABA-provider category the brief flags for caution; kept because it also runs public-awareness and policy-advocacy work and is Bulgaria's Autism-Europe affiliated member. Flagged here for editorial review.

name: auticon Canada
summary: Canadian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: Autism Canada
summary: National Canadian charity, marking its 50th anniversary in 2026, running a support line, an inclusive-employment training program and a community assistance program, describing its approach as advocating alongside autistic people and families.
notes: Founding year inferred from a stated 50th anniversary in 2026. Exact current headquarters city not confirmed on site (a Toronto-area phone number is listed); Guelph used per the organization's long-standing registered base.

name: Autism Nova Scotia
summary: Halifax-based community organization founded in October 2002 by parents of an autistic adult, building understanding, acceptance and inclusion for autistic people through advocacy, education and regional programming across Nova Scotia.
notes: Founded by Joan and Jack Craig, parents of an adult son with autism; board chaired by an autism consultant rather than an autistic self-advocate.

name: Autistics 4 Autistics Ontario
summary: Collective of autistic adults formed in 2017 that advocates for Ontario's autism policy and funding to shift from a charity model to a disability-rights model. An international affiliate of ASAN.
notes: International affiliate of the Autistic Self Advocacy Network (ASAN).

name: BC Hearing Voices Network
summary: A Vancouver-based peer network supporting people who hear voices, see visions, or have other unique sensory experiences, listed by Intervoice as Canada's hearing-voices contact.

name: Canadian ADHD Resource Alliance (CADDRA)
summary: Professional alliance of Canadian clinicians producing evidence-based ADHD practice guidelines, training materials and continuing education for healthcare providers, headquartered in the Toronto area.
notes: A clinician-run professional organization, not a patient self-advocacy group; site returns 403 to automated fetch (bot-filtering), confirmed live via curl headers.

name: Mad in Canada
summary: Canadian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, research summaries and lived-experience essays on science, psychiatry and social justice.
region: Toronto, ON (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network (parent: Mad in America). Editorial team composition and founding year not stated on the site.

name: Mad Pride Toronto
summary: The organising collective behind Toronto's annual Mad Pride Week, tracing back to the 1993 'Psychiatric Survivor Pride Day', the founding event of the international Mad Pride movement.
notes: Wikipedia identifies Toronto's Parkdale neighbourhood as the origin of the global Mad Pride movement, held annually except 1996.

name: Mad Studies Network
summary: International blog and network connecting scholars, psychiatric survivors and activists working in Mad Studies, sharing calls for papers, syllabi, and writing on madness from a critical, survivor-informed perspective.
notes: Blog/network associated with the Canadian Mad Studies scholarship tradition.

name: Quebec Federation of Autism (FQA)
summary: Montreal-based Quebec federation providing resources, training and tools for autistic adults, families and professionals, publishing materials and advocating on implementation of autism-related policy in Quebec.
notes: Site does not indicate whether autistic people hold leadership roles within the federation itself, hence ally-led rather than nd-led.

name: Sinneave Family Foundation
summary: Calgary-based Canadian operating foundation working with individuals, communities and organizations to reduce barriers to education, employment and housing for autistic youth and adults, running programs like NEUROinclusive Workforce Solutions and EmploymentWorks.
notes: Family-founded operating foundation; founding year not stated on site.

name: The Autism Acceptance Project (TAAP)
summary: Toronto nonprofit founded in 2006 by autism advocate and parent Estée Klar, promoting autism acceptance through arts programming, publications, and public education framed around neurodiversity rather than cure.
notes: Founded by a parent rather than an autistic person, though the project centers autistic voices in its arts and education programming. Site is JS-rendered; verified live via curl (200) rather than full content fetch.

name: Toronto Metropolitan University School of Disability Studies
summary: University department offering disability studies degrees including a Mad Studies stream, taught from a critical, anti-oppressive perspective on disability and psychiatric survivor history.
notes: Formerly Ryerson University.

name: FUAN - Autism and Neurodiversity Union Foundation
summary: A Chilean nonprofit combining autistic self-advocates and professionals that publishes public education on autism law, family mental health, and accessibility, and advocates on implementation of Chile's 2023 Autism Law.
notes: Exact headquarters city not confirmed on the public site; documented activity centers on the Valparaíso region. President Gabriela Verdugo Weinberger; team includes Chantal Garay Soto, also president of FENAUT (Federación Nacional de Autismo).

name: Mad Pride Chile (Orgullo Loco)
summary: A psychiatric survivor movement, active since 2015, that organizes Chile's annual Mad Pride marches and campaigns against practices like electroshock, reclaiming madness as an identity rather than an illness.
notes: Grew out of the Colectivo Autogestión Libre-Mente (founded 2014), a peer-support group of psychiatric service users/survivors meeting weekly at the Ailanto cultural center in Santiago. Instagram bio: 'Celebramos el derecho a la locura desde el año 2015'; also documented in academic literature.

name: Millennium Nucleus on Disability and Citizenship (DISCA)
summary: A Chilean state-funded interdisciplinary research center at Universidad Diego Portales studying disability and citizenship, using participatory methods with an advisory council of people with lived disability experience.
notes: Scope is disability studies broadly (physical, sensory, intellectual, psychosocial), not neurodiversity-exclusive, but includes research on psychiatric institutionalization and disabled youth activism. ANID-funded Millennium Nucleus, director Florencia Herrera.

name: Beijing Stars and Rain Education Institute for Autism
summary: China's first NGO dedicated to autistic children, founded in Beijing in 1993 by a parent, running an autism education and training programme for children and parents.
notes: Site intermittently unreachable, verified via Wikipedia/British Council. Older autismchina.org domain is now dead.

name: WABC Art Way (World of Art Brut Culture)
summary: Shanghai foundation, established in 2016 from a project begun in 2010, running free art courses and exhibitions for people with intellectual disabilities and autism to challenge public stigma through their creative work.
notes: Founder Miao Shiming began the initiative in 2010; formalized as a private non-public foundation in 2016; reports projects across more than 10 countries. Site intermittently returns server errors to HEAD requests but loads normally via GET.

name: AUTISCOL (Colombian Autistic People's Association)
summary: A Colombian association made up of adult autistic people that publishes self-advocacy writing on rights and neurodiversity, tracks pending autism-related legislation, and runs public petitions and reports.
notes: Explicitly self-describes as run by autistic people ('conformada por un grupo de autistas'). Also active on Substack (autiscol.substack.com) and Instagram (@autiscol). No fixed city/office found; coordinates approximate Bogotá as a placeholder for a national, largely online organization.

name: DISFAM Colombia
summary: The Colombian chapter of the international dyslexia/specific-learning-differences network DISFAM, doing advocacy and outreach for families and professionals and pushing regulation of Colombia's 2022 dyslexia law.
notes: Run by named regional representatives (Bogotá, Cali), not self-described as dyslexic-led. Most recent dated content is a December 2024 legislative working meeting on Colombia's dyslexia decree.

name: BarrileTEA
summary: San José nonprofit founded in November 2018 that campaigns for autism rights and legislation in Costa Rica. Known for its annual kite-flying 'BarrileTEAda' awareness events and its advocacy role in Costa Rica's 2021 Autism Law and 2024 implementing regulation.
notes: Official site barriletea.org was intermittently unresolvable on repeated checks, so the confirmed-live Facebook page is used as the primary url, with a 2024 elmundo.cr news article as source_url. Founder Jessica Varela's own neurodivergent status was not stated in available sources, so leadership is marked unknown rather than assumed.

name: Croatian Union of Associations for Autism (SUZAH)
summary: A Zagreb-based umbrella body coordinating 13 Croatian autism associations, tracing its roots to a 1979 parent group, running a helpline and advisory service and advocating for autistic people and families nationally.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding traced to the first Croatian parents-of-autistic-children group in 1979; current internal leadership composition not detailed on the site.

name: Autism Support Famagusta
summary: A Cypriot charity founded by parents and friends of autistic people near Famagusta, running a Summer Club since 2014, outreach and parent coffee mornings, and teacher-training seminars.
notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member; participates in the Pan Cypriot Autism Support Committee. Founding year not stated, though its Summer Club has run since 2014.

name: Adventor (A-komunita)
summary: Prague community centre and self-help organisation for autistic children, teenagers and adults, running individualised support, an antiquarian bookshop, and inclusion projects with mixed autistic and non-autistic teams.
notes: Runs the KC Kopec community centre. Full member of EUCAP. Site blocks bare curl requests (403) but is reachable with a browser user agent and was read in full via fetch.

name: Akrasia (Association for Adults with ADHD)
name_local: Spolek pro dospělé s diagnózou ADHD
summary: Czech association founded in 2022 by psychologists, some with personal ADHD experience, running a nationwide network of peer support groups, workshops and an online resource-navigation tool for adults with ADHD.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Also active in Brno and Pardubice.

name: European Council of Autistic People (EUCAP)
summary: An umbrella network of autistic-led organisations from across Europe that lobbies EU and national institutions, coordinates member groups, and represents autistic people in disability policy forums.
notes: Registered as 'European Council of Autistic People z.s.' in Prague, but is a pan-European body: 27 member organisations across 18 countries as of the source page. Prague is a legal registration address, not an operational hub; board and members are distributed across Europe.

name: Hearing Voices Network Czech Republic
summary: The Czech national node of the international Hearing Voices Network, listed by Intervoice as the Czech Republic's hearing-voices contact.

name: NAUTIS (National Institute for Autism)
summary: A Prague-based Czech national institute providing free counselling, diagnosis, therapy and training on autism, and running the AutismPort information portal, funded partly by EU and Czech government grants.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Grew out of APLA Praha, the organisation that founded the Pasparta publishing social enterprise; exact founding year not stated on the current site.

name: PASPARTA
summary: A Czech publishing house and social enterprise, founded by the autism organisation APLA Praha, that creates adapted graphic-design and publishing jobs for people with autism.
notes: Founded December 2012 by APLA Praha (now part of NAUTIS); publishes psychology, autism and special-education titles and offers graphic design services, employing people with autism in adapted roles. Cited as a good-practice example at the UN.

name: Autisme Ungdom
summary: Danish youth and disability organisation for autistic people aged 13-35, founded 2019 with a board composed entirely of young autistic people, running six regional chapters, a Discord community, and an annual summer camp.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP; found while cross-checking the EUCAP member list. Membership does not require a formal diagnosis.

name: Autisme- og Aspergerforeningen
summary: Danish national association describing itself as 'autisternes egen forening' (autistic people's own association), running local meeting places across the country, an annual Aukon conference, and disability-policy advocacy.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. No fixed single office; placed at a central Denmark coordinate. Automated curl checks returned a non-standard 454 status from this network; content was independently confirmed via fetch.

name: Hearing Voices Network Denmark
summary: Denmark's national Hearing Voices Network, listed by Intervoice, offering peer information and groups for voice-hearers.

name: Mad in Denmark
summary: Danish affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched around 2023, publishing critical-psychiatry articles and lived-experience accounts in Danish and English.
region: Copenhagen (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network. Launch year drawn from a Mad in the UK announcement post, not the site itself.

name: Ordblindeforeningen i Danmark
summary: Danish dyslexia association based in Taastrup, giving free professional guidance to individuals, schools and employers, running regional and youth chapters, and publishing a member magazine on dyslexia.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Patron since 2024 is Princess Marie of Denmark.

name: Specialisterne Foundation
summary: A Danish foundation, founded by the father of an autistic son, that places autistic and other neurodivergent people into paid jobs with partner companies through an assessment and training model.
notes: Founded by Thorkil Sonne; credited with creating roughly 10,000 jobs for autistic people globally through corporate partnerships (SAP, Microsoft, IBM and others). Included as a large, well-known anchor organisation; leadership is not itself predominantly neurodivergent-led.

name: World Network of Users and Survivors of Psychiatry (WNUSP)
summary: An international organisation of psychiatric survivors, founded in 1991 (as the World Federation of Psychiatric Users, renamed WNUSP in 1997), advocating for the rights of people labelled with mental illness within the UN human-rights system.
notes: Official domain wnusp.net is unreachable (connection refused) and wnusp.org now resolves to an unrelated retail site, so Wikipedia is used as both url and source_url. Wikipedia states WNUSP is based in Odense, Denmark since 2000 and is explicitly led by survivors of psychiatry.

name: Dominican Autism Foundation
summary: Santo Domingo nonprofit founded in 1999 and made up of parents of autistic children. Provides autism awareness education, a professional training diploma in neurodevelopmental-disorder evaluation, and support services for families.
notes: Site lists training sessions scheduled into 2026, indicating current activity; returns HTTP 406 to bare requests without browser headers (bot-filtering quirk, not a dead site). Membership explicitly described as the children's own parents, hence ally-led rather than nd-led.

name: Egyptian Autistic Society (EAS)
summary: Egyptian non-profit running four specialised centres offering education, therapy and workforce-training programmes, including a partnership with McDonald's Egypt, for autistic people and their families.
notes: Headquarters city not stated on site; Cairo used as a default for a nationally operating Egyptian NGO with four centres.

name: Learning Resource Center (LRC)
summary: Cairo centre founded in 1996 offering interdisciplinary diagnostic and therapeutic services for children with learning difficulties, developmental disorders and behavioural challenges, with a particular emphasis on autism and dyslexia.
notes: One of Egypt's longer-running interdisciplinary learning-disability/autism service centres; leadership and ownership structure not stated on the site.

name: Estonian Autism Alliance
summary: An umbrella organisation based in Tartu coordinating regional autism associations across Estonia, providing training and counselling to network members and advocating for autistic people's rights.
notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: MTÜ Autistid
summary: Estonian association, established 2019 as the Estonian Autistic Women's Association, that spreads information about autism and neurodiversity, builds community, and advocates to improve conditions for autistic people in Estonia.
notes: Full member of EUCAP, formerly Eesti Autistlike Naiste Ühing (Estonian Autistic Women's Association), founded 8 March 2019. Site notes it is under renovation. The EUCAP-listed URL (eany.ee) redirects to autistid.ee, used here. Leadership not explicitly stated on-site as autistic-led, so marked unknown despite the association's name and history.

name: Association of Different Learners (FINDER)
summary: Helsinki-based Finnish association supporting people with dyslexia, dyscalculia and other learning difficulties in work and education, offering counselling, peer 'experience expert' activities and policy advocacy.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association.

name: auticon Finland
summary: Finnish branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: Autism Foundation Finland
summary: A Helsinki-based Finnish foundation and KELA-approved service provider offering guidance, employment and education support, and 24-hour residential and supported housing for autistic people nationwide.
notes: Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member, distinct from the full-member Finnish Association for Autism and Asperger's Syndrome. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Finnish Association for Autism and Asperger's Syndrome
summary: Finland's national autism federation, coordinating member associations, publishing the quarterly Autismi-lehti magazine, and providing peer support, counselling and professional training nationwide.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Mad in Finland
summary: Finnish affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical mental-health journalism, event listings and a media-monitoring digest in Finnish.
region: Helsinki (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

name: Steg for Steg
summary: Finland's only Swedish-language association for and with people with intellectual disabilities, running nine local chapters, training members as experience speakers and campaigning on employment and accessibility.
notes: Site states the organisation is marking 30 years, suggesting founding around the mid-1990s (not confirmed precisely). Also has a base in Vaasa. Member of Finnish disability federation FDUV and of EPSA.

name: Suomen Autismikirjon Yhdistys (ASY)
summary: Helsinki-based Finnish association working for the wellbeing and equality of autistic people, running peer support groups, an autism-friendly certification programme, and summer and autumn community gatherings.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Leadership composition not explicitly stated as autistic-led on the pages read, so marked unknown despite EUCAP full-member status.

name: Suomen Moniääniset (Finnish Hearing Voices Network)
summary: Finland's national hearing-voices association, providing support to voice-hearers and their families and listed as Finland's Intervoice contact.
notes: Registered association ('ry').

name: Actions pour l'Autisme Asperger
summary: A French association founded in 2012 that fills gaps in Asperger diagnosis and support; half its volunteers are autistic themselves, and it runs the Aspiejob employment programme and helped set up five French diagnostic centres.
notes: Founded by Marie-Francoise Pere-Gaudio and Francine Stourdze; volunteers and board also active in Vincennes, Orleans, Alleins, Aix-en-Provence and Cassis.

name: Asperansa
summary: A Brittany association created by parents of children and young adults with Asperger syndrome and high-functioning autism, running monthly meeting cafes, social-skills groups, theatre and computer workshops in Brest.
notes: Direct verification via automated fetch was blocked by the site's Anubis bot-protection screen; existence and activity confirmed via Brittany's regional autism resource centre (CRA Bretagne) and the Ker'Aidants directory. Partner association of Autisme France.

name: Atypie-Friendly
summary: A French higher-education inclusion programme, coordinated since 2016 with Universite Grenoble Alpes among its founding members, supporting autistic and other neurodivergent students across a national network of partner universities.
notes: Originally launched as 'Aspie-Friendly' in 2016, later renamed 'Atypie-Friendly'. Spans many French universities; Grenoble used as coordinating base since Universite Grenoble Alpes is a founding member (joined 2018 per the site's own open data).

name: auticon France
summary: French branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: CLE Autistes
name_local: Collectif pour la Liberté d'Expression des Autistes
summary: A French self-advocacy collective, run entirely by autistic people, that organises peer support, training and campaigns and treats autism as a political identity rather than only a diagnosis.
notes: Founded September 2018; over 130 members and 400 supporters nationally. Governed by a collegial leadership composed entirely of autistic people, renewed by co-optation.

name: Compagnie de l'Oiseau-Mouche
summary: Roubaix theatre company founded in 1978 (professionalized 1981) as France's first artistic ESAT, with a permanent troupe of actors with intellectual/psychological disability directed by rotating outside stage directors.
notes: General/artistic direction held by non-disabled staff; productions staged by guest directors. Permanent troupe of ~20-23 comédien·ne·s have intellectual/psychological disability.

name: French Federation of Dys Disorders (FFDys)
summary: French federation of regional associations for people with dyslexia, dyspraxia, dyscalculia and related developmental disorders, running an annual National Dys Day and professional training programme.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Its 20th National Dys Day fell in 2026. Site describes mobilising 'parents and professionals throughout France,' hence marked ally-led.

name: Nous Aussi
summary: A French self-advocacy association of and for people with intellectual disabilities, led by members themselves under the motto 'Rien pour nous, sans nous', training local delegates and producing easy-to-read civic material.
notes: Member of the European Platform of Self-Advocates (EPSA). Held its 2025 general assembly in Paris and 2024 national congress in Dunkerque; no single confirmed HQ city, Paris used as anchor. Distinct from an unrelated same-named service provider at nousaussi.fr in Haute-Savoie.

name: REV France (Hearing Voices Network France)
name_local: Réseau français sur l'Entente de Voix
summary: France's national Hearing Voices Network, coordinating peer support groups for voice-hearers and listed as France's Intervoice contact.

name: Aspies e.V.
summary: The oldest and largest German self-help association for autistic adults, run by an all-autistic board, offering local peer groups nationwide, a crisis helpline and an online self-help forum.
notes: Around 550 members, board of five autistic people, registered at Berlin-Charlottenburg district court. Member of EUCAP. Automated HTTPS checks from this session failed with a TLS renegotiation error against aspies.de specifically; live page content was independently confirmed via a fetch tool, so it is not treated as down.

name: Atelier Goldstein
summary: An artist studio in Frankfurt, Germany, founded in 2001 as a project of Lebenshilfe Frankfurt, offering individual artistic assistance from professional artists to people with cognitive disabilities; work has shown at documenta fifteen and Schirn Kunsthalle.
notes: Site's WAF returns HTTP 500 on plain HEAD requests but 200 on GET (verified live via GET and WebFetch).

name: auticon Germany
summary: German headquarters of auticon, an IT and business consultancy that employs autistic people as consultants and provides workplace coaching and employer training on neuroinclusion.
notes: Founded by Dirk Müller-Remus, whose son is autistic; part of the international auticon network.

name: Autismus-Kultur
summary: German website written from an autistic perspective on how autistic people can live well in a non-autistic world, offering practical guidance, tips and community discussion rather than clinical advice.
notes: Site self-describes as written from an autistic perspective. Returns 403 to automated fetches (bot-blocking); reachable and returns 200 to a plain curl with a browser user agent. No stated headquarters city; placed at a geographic-centre-of-Germany coordinate as a placeholder.

name: autSocial e.V.
summary: Hamburg-based German association run under the motto 'von Autist*innen für Autist*innen' (by autistic people for autistic people), operating self-help groups, online workshops on masking and workplace inclusion, and creative projects like autArt.
notes: Full member of EUCAP; funded in part through Hamburg's social affairs authority.

name: Federal Association for Dyslexia and Dyscalculia (BVL)
summary: German federal association, established around 1976, advocating for accommodations for people with dyslexia and dyscalculia in school, training and careers, with regional chapters and a therapist certification programme.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Founding year inferred from the site's own '50 years' anniversary claim.

name: Kunstwerkstatt der Lebenshilfe Berlin
summary: An inclusive art workshop run by Lebenshilfe Berlin in Berlin, Germany, active since at least 1999 (its first exhibition), where professional facilitators guide clients with intellectual disabilities in painting and other visual art.
notes: Domain works reliably only over plain HTTP; HTTPS fails TLS handshake. Exact founding year not stated on-site — earliest documented activity is its 1999 exhibition.

name: Mad in Germany
summary: German affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry essays, translated international pieces and lived-experience accounts in German.
region: Berlin (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

name: Netzwerk Stimmenhören (German Hearing Voices Network)
summary: Germany's national Hearing Voices Network association, coordinating peer groups and information on hearing voices, listed as Germany's Intervoice contact.
notes: Registered association ('e.V.'). Old domain netzwerk-stimmenhoeren.de now redirects here.

name: Prinzhorn Collection
summary: Collection of art by psychiatric patients assembled by Hans Prinzhorn at Heidelberg University's psychiatric clinic from 1919, with a dedicated museum inaugurated in 2001; now ~40,000 works from 1825 to today.
notes: Part of Heidelberg University Hospital; a research/curatorial institution, not patient- or artist-run.

name: Theater Thikwa
summary: Berlin theatre company founded in 1991, self-described as a company where artists 'with and without disability' make theatre together; artistic direction is currently shared by Nicole Hummel and Laura Besch.

name: Autism Awareness Care and Training Centre (AACT)
summary: Accra-based centre for autistic children founded in 1998 by a nurse practitioner and parent, providing behaviour management, therapy, and individualized education plans.
notes: Parent-led, professionally run. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent; needs a full browser-style header.

name: BasicNeeds-Ghana
summary: Ghanaian implementation of the BasicNeeds mental-health-and-development model, involving people with mental illness or epilepsy and their families directly in community mental-health services, livelihoods support, and policy advocacy.
notes: Operates across multiple Ghanaian communities beyond the capital; exact headquarters city and founding year not stated on the site. Sister programme to BasicNeeds/BNBR in Kenya.

name: Greek Society for the Protection of Autistic People (GSPAP)
summary: Founded in Athens in November 1992 by 80 parents of autistic people from Athens, Piraeus and Crete, this national society runs residential and day-centre services in Attica, Macedonia and Ioannina.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Explicitly parent-founded; current governance not detailed on the site.

name: Hearing Voices Network Greece
summary: Greece's national Hearing Voices Network, offering peer information and groups for voice-hearers and listed as Greece's Intervoice contact.

name: Mad in Greece
summary: Greek affiliate of the Mad in the World network, run by a volunteer contributor team publishing psychopharmaceutical-policy critique, personal narratives and art on psychiatric experience.
region: Athens (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Site names a volunteer team page ('Our Team') and invites contributions; individual members' lived-experience status not confirmed, hence 'mixed' rather than 'nd-led'.

name: Hong Kong Autism Institute
summary: Hong Kong non-profit company working on autism knowledge development and public engagement, including organising local World Autism Awareness Day activities.
notes: Limited public detail on founding date or leadership; site content centers on knowledge resources and World Autism Awareness Day.

name: NeuroDiversity Association Hong Kong (NDAHK)
summary: Hong Kong advocacy organisation, established in 2024, promoting the value of neurodiversity through cross-sector partnerships, education, and conferences.

name: Special Needs Network Hong Kong (SNNHK)
summary: Volunteer-run peer network connecting parents and caregivers of children with neurodiversity and disabilities in Hong Kong through events, workshops and information sharing.
notes: Membership is exclusive to parents and caregivers; run by a volunteer committee, not a professional service provider.

name: Talos Foundation
summary: Hong Kong charity founded in 2021 running neurodiversity-awareness campaigns, corporate training and employment-inclusion programmes for autistic and other neurodivergent people.
notes: Founded by Mary Schaus after her son's autism diagnosis, per South China Morning Post coverage; a Section 88 charitable organisation.

name: Hungarian Autistic Society (AOSZ)
summary: Hungary's national autism federation, based in Budapest, listed as a full member of Autism-Europe representing autistic people and their families in national advocacy.
notes: The live site is currently a bare landing page with no navigable content, so facts are drawn from Autism-Europe's official August 2026 member directory rather than the org's own site. Founding year and leadership composition unconfirmed.

name: Mars Foundation
summary: A Budapest foundation for autism awareness offering family and professional training, downloadable social-story resources, a parent support club, and urban life-skills training for autistic teenagers.
notes: Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member. Runs Erasmus+ international projects; founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Einhverfusamtökin (Icelandic Autism Association)
summary: Iceland's national autism association, based in Reykjavik, providing autism education resources, rights and benefits information, and social groups for autistic youth and adults in Reykjavik and Akureyri.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Hugarafl
summary: A Reykjavik peer-run mental-health community offering recovery, empowerment and hearing-voices support groups run by and for its members; Iceland's Intervoice contact.
notes: Site describes itself as 'samfélag jafningja sem styðja hvert annað' (a community of peers who support one another); broader peer mental-health community whose activities include the Icelandic hearing-voices group.

name: Action for Autism (AFA) - National Centre for Autism
summary: Delhi-based Indian non-profit, founded in 1991 as a parent support group, running assessment, education, therapy, employment, and self-advocacy services for autistic people.
notes: Runs a Self-Advocacy Programme, but it is professionally facilitated rather than self-advocate-run.

name: Autism Society West Bengal
summary: Kolkata parent-initiated nonprofit, around 20 years old, providing early intervention, assessment and an RCI-certified special-educator training diploma for the autism community.
notes: Site marks a 20th-anniversary milestone as of 2026, suggesting founding around 2006; not independently dated.

name: Bapu Trust for Research on Mind & Discourse
summary: Pune-based trust doing non-coercive, community-based mental health work, including an urban community mental health and inclusion programme; founder was active in the international Hearing Voices movement.
notes: About page 404'd during verification; leadership framing not explicitly self-declared. Site returns 406 to a bare curl user agent.

name: Forum For Autism
summary: Mumbai parent-support trust, founded in 2001, running a specialised library and peer network for families of autistic people, with about 350 members drawn from parents and professionals.

name: India Autism Center (IAC)
summary: Section 8 non-profit near Kolkata founded by an entrepreneur whose son is autistic, building a residential campus alongside training and research divisions for autism support across India.
