notes: Founder Suresh Kumar Somani; residential campus (Samaavesh) scheduled to open in early 2027.

name: Mad in South Asia
summary: Regional affiliate of the Mad in the World network covering India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Bhutan and Nepal, run by a core team of therapists, researchers, professors and psychiatric-service users who center survivors' own accounts.
region: Pune, Maharashtra (approximate anchor; site states no single national HQ)
notes: Regional, not single-country; India used only as an approximate map anchor given the site's connections to Pune-based Bapu Trust and lack of a stated HQ city. Site explicitly states service users/survivors are kept 'first' among contributors.

name: Madras Dyslexia Association (MDA)
summary: Chennai non-profit founded in 1992 by parents, educationists and philanthropists that provides dyslexia assessment, remediation, teacher training and school resource-room support.

name: Sethu
summary: Goa trust, registered in 2005, running a neurodiversity-affirming child-development and family-guidance centre for children with autism, ADHD, dyslexia and other developmental disabilities.
notes: Describes its approach as neurodiversity-affirming and strengths-based rather than purely clinical; uses a family-centered 'Trifecta Model'.

name: TCI Global (Transforming Communities for Inclusion)
summary: A global federation of organisations of persons with psychosocial disabilities, grown since 2012 from an Asia-Pacific network supported by Pune's Bapu Trust and the International Disability Alliance, campaigning to abolish coercive mental-health law.
region: Pune, Maharashtra (originating hub; now a global federation)
notes: Explicitly self-describes as 'a global Organisation of persons with psychosocial disabilities [an OPD]'. Originated as the 'TransAsian strategy group' (2012-2014) working with Bapu Trust, already in the atlas. The domain tci-asia.org, once its Asia-Pacific site, now resolves to an unrelated gambling site and should not be used.

name: Ummeed Child Development Center
summary: Mumbai-based non-profit founded in 2001 by a developmental pediatrician, providing trans-disciplinary clinical services, training, and research for children with developmental disabilities.

name: Vidya Sagar
summary: Chennai disability organisation, formerly the Spastic Society of India, with over 40 years of early intervention, education, therapy, vocational training and rights advocacy across disability types including autism.
notes: Renamed from the Spastic Society of India; frames itself around 'disability is a part of human diversity' rather than a purely medical model.

name: Rumah Autis
summary: Indonesian foundation founded in 2004 providing low-cost or free therapy and schooling for autistic children and other children with special needs, now operating multiple branches.
notes: Operates under Yayasan Cahaya Keluarga Fitrah; headquarters city drawn from secondary reporting, not independently reconfirmed on the site itself this session.

name: Yayasan MPATI (Masyarakat Peduli Autis Indonesia)
summary: Indonesian national foundation, evolved from a 1998 parent community, focused on training and empowering parents of autistic children and advocating for government autism support policy.
notes: Evolved from KOMPAA (Komunitas Peduli Autis dan ADHD), founded in 1998.

name: Anjoman Autism Iran (Iran Autism Association)
summary: Tehran-based NGO and Iran's only nationally licensed autism association, running 23 regional offices that provide diagnosis, rehabilitation, family counselling and policy advocacy for autistic people.
notes: Holds UN ECOSOC consultative status and government-ministry licensing per its own site.

name: AsIAm
summary: Ireland's national autism charity, founded in 2014 by autistic CEO Adam Harris, working on autism-friendly community certification, policy and self-advocacy, with a stated policy of at least half its board being autistic.
notes: Registered as a Disabled Persons' Organisation; runs the Autism Friendly Towns programme.

name: Autistic Doctors International
summary: International peer network of autistic physicians and medical students founded by an autistic consultant anaesthetist, supporting members and publishing research on autistic doctors' experiences.
notes: Founder is an autistic physician; group is explicitly by and for autistic doctors.

name: Dyslexia Ireland
summary: Dublin-based Irish charity providing dyslexia and dyscalculia assessments, tutoring, training for parents and teachers, and policy advocacy, funded in part by the Department of Education.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Site returns 403 to some automated fetch tools (bot-blocking) but was read in full via a different fetch and confirmed live with a browser-header curl.

name: Hearing Voices Network Ireland
summary: Ireland's national Hearing Voices Network, coordinating local peer groups and training, historically linked to academics Harry Gijbels and Lydia Sapouna at University College Cork.
notes: Distinct from the editorial site Mad in Ireland (madinireland.com), already in the atlas; both trace to the same UCC-linked circle of academics and voice-hearers.

name: Mad in Ireland
summary: An Irish collective of psychiatric survivors, peer workers, academics and practitioners that publishes critical commentary and organises events challenging the dominant diagnostic model in mental health care.
notes: An affiliate of the international Mad in the World network. Governing team includes psychiatric survivors/peer support leaders alongside mental health practitioners and academics.

name: ALUT - The Israeli Society for Autistic Children and Adults
summary: Israel's national autism association, providing lifelong therapeutic, educational and residential services for autistic people through a nationwide network of centres.
notes: Site blocked automated content extraction during verification; live status confirmed via direct HTTP check (200) only, so founding year and details are left unconfirmed.

name: Beit Issie Shapiro
summary: Israeli nonprofit that develops, researches, and scales disability service models such as early intervention and assistive technology, and shares them internationally.
notes: Holds UN ECOSOC consultative status.

name: Bizchut - The Israel Human Rights Center for People with Disabilities
summary: Independent legal-advocacy and watchdog organisation advancing the rights of people with all disability types in Israel through litigation, policy work, and a public inquiries hotline.
notes: Cross-disability, not neurodiversity-specific; board combines disabled people, parents, professionals, and academics.

name: Enosh - The Israeli Mental Health Association
summary: Israeli non-profit operating roughly 96 centres nationwide offering mental-health rehabilitation, housing, employment and family-support services for people living with mental illness.
notes: Primarily a large-scale service-delivery organisation rather than a self-advocacy movement group; included for its national scale in Israeli mental-health rehabilitation and family support.

name: Shutaf Inclusion Programs
summary: Jerusalem-based "reverse inclusion" nonprofit running year-round camps and youth-leadership programs where disabled and non-disabled children and teens participate together.
notes: Direct page fetch was blocked by a bot filter; verified live via curl (200 OK) and secondary sources.

name: ARCI Intervoice Italia
name_local: ARCI Intervoice Italia APS (formerly Rete Italiana Noi e le Voci)
summary: Italy's national Hearing Voices association, offering information and peer exchange for voice-hearers, professionals and relatives, treating hearing voices as a human experience rather than a symptom.
region: Italy (national association; HQ city not stated)
notes: Rebranded from 'Rete Italiana Noi e le Voci' (parlaconlevoci.it, now a redirect page) to ARCI Intervoice Italia APS. Registered as an Italian APS (Associazione di Promozione Sociale).

name: Aspergeronline
summary: An Italian association founded by an autistic designer that offers self-screening tools, peer community, a podcast and resources for autistic people and professionals, built with an autistic development team.
notes: Founded January 2023 by Simone Favarin, an autistic designer and communicator; became a formal association (ETS) in December 2023. Reports 356,817 unique users and 60,000+ RAADS-R screenings completed in 2024.

name: auticon Italy
summary: Italian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: Gruppo Asperger APS
summary: An Italian association founded in 2003, with volunteers described as predominantly autistic themselves, that supports autistic people nationally and helped found regional Asperger groups in eight Italian regions.
notes: Became an APS (association of social promotion) in July 2025, after founding as an Onlus in 2003. Distinct from the Rome-based Spazio Asperger. Helped establish regional groups in Abruzzo, Campania, Emilia-Romagna, Lazio, Liguria, Lombardia, Piemonte and Veneto.

name: Gruppo Asperger Campania
summary: A Naples-based nonprofit, registered in Italy's national third-sector register, that is the Campania regional partner of Gruppo Asperger APS supporting autistic people and families.
notes: Registered in RUNTS (Registro Unico Nazionale del Terzo Settore) under number 36578. Founding date and leadership composition not stated on-site.

name: Gruppo Asperger Lazio
summary: A Rome-region volunteer association for autistic people and families, running school-inclusion projects, parent coaching, film festivals and the decade-old Autistic Football Club, a regional partner of Gruppo Asperger APS.
notes: Activity dates back to at least 2014; also active in Viterbo, Ferentino and Colonna. Distinct organisation from the Rome-based Spazio Asperger.

name: Gruppo Asperger Veneto
summary: A Verona-based volunteer organisation, founded in 2016, focused on level-1 ('Asperger') autism, running school and workplace training, post-diagnosis guidance and support networks for families across the Veneto region.
notes: Runs 'Progetto Decollo' post-diagnosis guidance and dedicated projects for girls/women and fathers. A regional partner of Gruppo Asperger APS.

name: Italian Dyslexia Association (AID)
summary: Bologna-based Italian association, founded 1997, supporting people with specific learning disorders across their lifespan through teacher and family training, the LibroAID digital textbook platform, and school/workplace advocacy.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association.

name: La Collina
summary: A Trieste work-integration cooperative founded in 1988 out of Franco Basaglia's psychiatric reform movement, employing people excluded from the labour market in restaurants, a hotel, museum and administrative services.
notes: A type A+B social cooperative; manages Radio Fragola among its cultural projects. Still active in 2026 per its own news page.

name: Mad in Italy
summary: Italian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, founded in 2018 and run by a mixed board of a psychiatrist, a pharmacology researcher and two psychiatric-survivor advocates.
region: Rome (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Board includes Susanna Brunelli and Cristina Paderi, both self-described psychiatric-survivor advocates, alongside a psychiatrist and a pharmacology researcher.

name: Neuropeculiar
summary: Italian association founded and directed by autistic people that campaigns for self-representation and self-determination under a neurodiversity and Disability Studies framework, and organises the annual AUTcamp gathering.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. No single stated headquarters; located at Rome, where its 2026 AUTcamp event is held.

name: Radio Fragola
summary: A community radio station broadcasting since 1984 from the former San Giovanni psychiatric hospital in Trieste, run by the social cooperative La Collina in the lineage of Franco Basaglia's psychiatric reform.
notes: Grew out of Italy's free-radio movement following the 1978 Basaglia Law that closed psychiatric hospitals; managed by Cooperativa Sociale La Collina; founded the 'Larghe Vedute' mental-health radio network in 2015.

name: Radio Fragola Gorizia
summary: A sister station to Trieste's Radio Fragola, launched in 2016 in Gorizia's Parco Basaglia, producing documentaries, audio dramas and community radio events in the same psychiatric-reform lineage.
notes: Operates from 'Area 174' in Gorizia's Parco Basaglia, extending the Trieste model; hosts the 'Frontiere dei lunatici' festival programme.

name: Spazio Asperger
summary: A Rome-based nonprofit for neurodivergent people running a weekly film club, theatre productions, a listening/support service and publishing, under the motto 'embrace neurodiversity'.
notes: Runs 'Aspie Saturday Film' weekly screenings and is linked to CuoreMenteLab, a clinical centre for neurodiversity.

name: Able Art Japan
name_local: エイブル・アート・ジャパン
summary: Able Art Japan is a Tokyo NPO founded in 1995 that supports people with disabilities in creating, exhibiting, and selling art; it co-founded the affiliated Able Art Company (2007), an agency licensing disabled artists' work commercially.
notes: Related entity Able Art Company (https://ableartcom.jp/, curl 200 OK) is an artist agency founded 2007 by three Japanese NPOs including Able Art Japan, HQ in Nara with a Tokyo office. Neither site explicitly claims artist-led governance; language is 'together with people with disabilities.'

name: Atelier Incurve
summary: Atelier Incurve (renamed INCURVE in April 2024) is a licensed day-service art facility in Osaka operated by the Social Welfare Corporation Sou-kai for adults with intellectual disabilities under Japan's disability-support law.
notes: Site confirms operation by Social Welfare Corporation Sou-kai and the 2024 rename to INCURVE, but does not state the studio's original founding year on pages checked.

name: EDGE (Japan Dyslexia Society)
name_local: 特定非営利活動法人エッジ
summary: Tokyo NPO founded in 2001 to promote correct understanding of dyslexia in Japan, training teachers, publishing guidance and running instructional courses for people with reading and writing difficulties.
notes: Name is an acronym for 'Japan Dyslexia Society'; runs teacher-training courses and public education on developmental dyslexia.

name: Hattatsu Kyokai (Developmental Disorders Association)
name_local: 公益社団法人発達協会
summary: Tokyo public-interest association, incorporated in 1982 out of an earlier parent and therapist self-help group, running a clinic, therapeutic programmes and publications for children and adults with developmental disabilities.
notes: Grew out of an earlier therapeutic self-help group; runs the Oji Clinic and a monthly magazine.

name: Japan Developmental Disabilities Network (JDDnet)
name_local: 日本発達障害ネットワーク
summary: Tokyo-based umbrella network of about 57 affiliated parent groups, academic societies, and professional bodies covering autism, ADHD, and learning disabilities nationally in Japan.
notes: Founded following Japan's 2004 Developmental Disabilities Support Law.

name: Japan Developmental Disability Advocates Association (JDDA)
summary: Peer-led Japanese association founded in 2015 that advocates on policy affecting people with developmental disabilities, including ADHD medication shortages, and trains peer-support group leaders.
notes: Distinct from the larger ally/professional umbrella network JDDnet; describes itself as working through the voices of people with developmental disabilities themselves, including lobbying Japan's health ministry on Concerta access.

name: Tojisha-Kenkyu Network
name_local: 当事者研究ネットワーク
summary: Japanese network coordinating tojisha-kenkyu, a method in which people with disabilities, mental illness or addiction research and theorize their own experience collaboratively rather than being studied by outsiders.
notes: Tojisha-kenkyu ('research by the person concerned') originated at Bethel House and is associated with researcher Shin'ichiro Kumagaya at the University of Tokyo.

name: Urakawa Bethel House
summary: Social welfare corporation in Hokkaido founded in 1984 by former psychiatric patients and a social worker, practicing "Tojisha-Kenkyu" (self-directed peer research) into members' own psychiatric experiences.
notes: Explicitly by-and-for psychiatric survivors (tojisha); runs an annual 'Bethel Festival' and cooperative small businesses.

name: ADHD Jersey
summary: Jersey (Channel Islands) not-for-profit combining lived ADHD experience with professional expertise, running adult and youth ADHD support programmes, awareness talks and a community hub in St Helier.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. Site states it was 'built by people who truly understand ADHD because we've lived it,' combined with professional expertise.

name: Autism in Kazakhstan (information platform)
summary: Kazakhstani information and analysis platform, launched around 2020-2021, publishing material on autism diagnosis, genetics and interventions for families.
notes: Primarily an informational/media platform rather than a direct-service or advocacy organisation; headquarters city not stated on site, Almaty used as a default for a national online project.

name: Basic Needs Basic Rights Kenya (BNBR Kenya)
summary: Nairobi-headquartered mental-health and psychosocial-disability organisation, roughly two decades old, running the community-based BasicNeeds mental-health-and-development model across several Kenyan counties and campaigning for policy change.
notes: Explicitly aims to 'directly involve people with mental illness or epilepsy, and their families and communities' in programme design. Also runs offices in Bungoma and Kilifi counties; part of the wider BasicNeeds network also active in Ghana.

name: Dyslexia Organisation Kenya (DOK)
summary: Nairobi nonprofit founded in 2010 advancing inclusive education through dyslexia screening, formal assessment, teacher training and neurodiversity awareness; operates the Rare Gem Talent School for neurodivergent children.
notes: Directed by Nancy Munyi via the affiliated Rare Gem Talent School; not stated as dyslexic-led.

name: Kenya Association of the Intellectually Handicapped (KAIH)
summary: Nairobi rights organisation promoting human rights of people with intellectual disabilities and their families through self-advocacy programmes, access-to-justice work, and evidence-based policy advocacy.
notes: Site current as of November 2024 news posts; partners with the Government of Kenya and the Kenya National Commission on Human Rights. Note: the shorter domain kaih.co.ke serves only a private care-dashboard login, kaihid.org is the informational site.

name: Latvian Autism Association
summary: A Riga-based association founded on 1 October 2006 to protect the rights and interests of autistic people in Latvia, running a psychosocial rehabilitation programme for children and joining Autism-Europe in 2013.
notes: Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member (joined 2013). Chaired by Līga Bērziņa as of the source page; leadership composition (parent-led vs. self-advocate) not explicitly stated.

name: Lebanese Autism Society (LAS)
summary: Beirut-based membership NGO founded by parents and professionals, running educational, vocational, and consultancy programs for autistic children and teens.
notes: Runs a Technical School for Adolescents with Autism.

name: Rain Children
summary: A Vilnius-based Lithuanian nonprofit uniting families of autistic children, autistic adults and professionals, running a resource directory, peer-support groups for autistic youth, and a community handmade-goods shop.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Site references '10 years' of operation without giving an exact founding date; unites families, adults with autism, and professionals rather than being purely parent-led.

name: Fondation Autisme Luxembourg (FAL)
summary: A Luxembourg foundation, marking its 30th anniversary in 2026, providing residential care at five sites for 39 autistic residents, family support to about 650 families, and professional training on autism.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year (1996) inferred from a 30th-anniversary reference on the site in 2026.

name: Malaysian Autism Resource Foundation (MARF)
summary: Malaysian foundation providing resources, caregiver empowerment and advocacy for autistic individuals and their families, including autism-friendly community initiatives.

name: National Autism Society of Malaysia (NASOM)
summary: Malaysia's longest-running national autism body, founded in 1986, running early intervention, therapy, vocational training, and residential independent-living programmes nationwide.

name: United Voice
name_local: Persatuan Advokasi Diri Orang Bermasalah Pembelajaran Selangor & Kuala Lumpur
summary: The first Malaysian society run by persons with learning disabilities themselves, founded in 2005, delivering self-advocacy training and a supported-employment project for its members.
notes: Members include people with Down syndrome, autism, ADHD and other learning disabilities; registered with Malaysia's Registrar of Societies in July 2005.

name: Autism Parents Association (APA)
summary: A Maltese voluntary organisation of over 450 member families of autistic children, running a private peer-support network, an autism handbook, seminars, and the SIPT sensory-integration youth programme.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe, registered as voluntary organisation VO802. Founded by parents of autistic children; founding year not stated on the site.

name: Hearing Voices Network Malta
summary: Malta's national Hearing Voices peer group, listed by Intervoice as the country's national contact for hearing-voices support.
notes: Only public presence is this Wix site; no separate domain found.

name: Autisme Maurice
summary: Mauritian NGO, registered in 2010 (founded 2009) as successor to the Autism Intervention Association, providing counselling, needs assessment, diagnostic services via SEDAM at Wellkin Hospital, and professional training on autism.
notes: Registered as an approved NGO by Mauritius's National Empowerment Foundation. Committee-governed; not stated as autistic-led.

name: Autistas de México
summary: Mexico City organization that describes itself as the first association in Mexico created by and for autistic people. Offers autism/ADHD differential diagnosis, therapy and coaching delivered by autistic staff, plus community support groups, reaching clients nationwide online.
notes: Self-description confirmed verbatim on site: 'la primera asociación en México creada por y para autistas.' Also participates in the Marcha del Orgullo Loco. Founding year not stated precisely, left null rather than guessed. Charges for clinical/diagnostic services alongside its community/advocacy work.

name: Colectivo Chuhcan
summary: Mexico City civil association founded in 2011 and run entirely by people with lived experience of psychiatric diagnosis. Provides peer support, human-rights advocacy against forced institutionalization, and helped organize Mexico's first Mad Pride march.
notes: No independent Chuhcan website or confirmed social-media handle was found; url/source_url point to a Mad in Mexico interview with founder Raúl Montoya. Also active in Red Orgullo Loco México's annual Marcha del Orgullo Loco alongside other user-led collectives (SinColectivo, Colectiva Meteorita) that could not be independently verified.

name: Yo También
summary: Mexican civil association working on educational and labor inclusion for people with intellectual disabilities, including Down syndrome, through training and workplace-integration programmes.

name: SOS Autism Moldova
summary: A Chișinău-based Moldovan association founded in May 2008 by parents of autistic children, offering ABA, speech and art therapy, and acting as the main advocate to national authorities on autism policy.
notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member. Explicitly founded by a group of parents of autistic children.

name: Autism Association of Namibia
summary: Windhoek-based volunteer association of parents, autistic adults and professionals promoting the wellbeing of people with autism spectrum conditions in Namibia through support, training and awareness activities.
notes: Explicitly describes itself as run by 'parents, their children with ASC, adults with ASC and professionals' on a volunteer basis. Seeking funding for an assessment centre.

name: AutismCare Nepal Society (ACNS)
summary: Parent-run Nepali NGO, founded on World Autism Awareness Day 2008, providing diagnosis, early intervention, schooling and vocational training for autistic people from its Lalitpur base.

name: Autistic Welfare Association Nepal (AWAN)
summary: Kathmandu non-profit with over 15 years of operation providing behavioural training, financial assistance and educational support to children and adults with autism and intellectual disabilities.

name: Atelier Herenplaats
summary: An art studio and gallery in Rotterdam, Netherlands, founded in 1991, providing studio space and training for about 35 artists with intellectual disabilities or psychiatric backgrounds, supervised by professional artists and art teachers.

name: Autminds
summary: Dutch congress for and by autistic people, run for eleven years out of Delft, bringing autistic adults together for talks, workshops and networking; its final edition is scheduled for October 2026.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Founding year inferred from the site's own '11 years' claim ahead of its announced final October 2026 congress; included despite the planned wind-down because it is still active as of verification.

name: European Network of (Ex-)Users and Survivors of Psychiatry (ENUSP)
summary: A grassroots umbrella organisation, founded in 1990 by Dutch psychiatric survivors, uniting national and local user/survivor organisations across Europe to advocate directly on human rights in mental health.
region: Netherlands (founding country; no fixed current HQ stated)
notes: Site states: 'We directly represent the views of people who are or have been on the receiving end of psychiatric services' and describes itself as the only grassroots umbrella working across Europe on this basis. No current registered-office city found; located here at its 1990 founding country only.

name: LFB
name_local: Belangenvereniging van mensen met een verstandelijke beperking
summary: The Dutch national advocacy organisation by and for people with intellectual disabilities, based in Utrecht with offices in twelve cities, training members as paid 'experience experts' and advising policymakers.
notes: Member of the European Platform of Self-Advocates (EPSA). Runs the STERKopleiding training programme and STERKplaatsen community centres; regional offices also in Assen, Emmeloord, Goes, Groningen, Haarlem, Heerlen, Leeuwarden, Nijmegen, Rotterdam, Twente and Wolvega.

name: Mad in the Netherlands
summary: Dutch affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched 1 February 2022 as the tenth national affiliate, making international critical-psychiatry and psychopharmacology knowledge accessible in Dutch.
region: Amsterdam (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

name: PAS Nederland
summary: A Dutch peer-run association for people with autism and average-to-high intelligence, mostly staffed by autistic board members and volunteers, running local groups in several Dutch cities.
notes: Activities run in multiple cities including Alkmaar, Utrecht, Nijmegen, Weert, 's-Hertogenbosch, Leiden and Zwolle; The Hague used as the organisation's registered base.

name: Stichting Weerklank
summary: The Dutch national Hearing Voices foundation, supporting people who hear voices, see visions or have other unusual perceptions, and their relatives, and listed as the Netherlands' Intervoice contact.

name: ADHD New Zealand
summary: New Zealand charity, funded entirely by donations with no government funding, providing information, self-screening tools, webinars and peer support for people with ADHD and their whanau.

name: Altogether Autism
summary: Free, government-funded nationwide autism information and advisory service for autistic people, whanau, and professionals in New Zealand.
notes: Run in partnership between Your Way | Kia Roha and Parent to Parent New Zealand; includes an autistic-led peer offshoot, 'By Autistics for Autistics'.

name: Autism New Zealand
summary: National New Zealand charity supporting autistic people and their families through a Board of Trustees and nationwide services.
notes: At least one board member is autistic and also a parent of an autistic adult; overall composition reads as ally-led/mixed.

name: Dyslexia Foundation of New Zealand
summary: New Zealand charitable trust, established in 2006, running a dyslexia knowledge hub with practical guidance and lived-experience accounts for homes, classrooms and workplaces.
region: New Zealand (national, no fixed HQ city stated)

name: Hearing Voices Network Aotearoa New Zealand
summary: New Zealand's national Hearing Voices Network, providing information and peer group support for voice-hearers and listed as the country's Intervoice contact.

name: Tourette's Association of New Zealand
summary: New Zealand charity raising Tourette syndrome awareness and running public-education campaigns, including Tourette's Awareness Month activities.
region: New Zealand (national, no fixed HQ city stated)
notes: Headquarters city not stated on site.

name: Dyslexia Foundation Nigeria
summary: Nigerian nonprofit founded in 2015 by a couple who sought dyslexia services abroad for their child. Offers the country's first comprehensive dyslexia assessment and diagnosis service, plus training for educators, administrators and parents.
notes: Co-founders Felicia and Ben Arikpo serve as Executive Director and Executive Chairman. Offices in both Lagos and Abuja.

name: Ike Foundation for Autism (IFA)
summary: Abuja-based foundation providing an early-intervention centre, a healthcare centre, and professional training for caregivers, parents and therapists of autistic children.
notes: Leadership composition and founding year not stated on the site.

name: Mentally Aware Nigeria Initiative (MANI)
summary: Lagos-headquartered, youth-run mental-health network founded in 2015 by Dr Victor Ugo after his own depression diagnosis. Runs free counselling, a helpline, and mental-health training across 18 chapters and reports direct support to over 70,000 people.
notes: Describes itself as 'youth-run and youth-focused'; largest youth mental-health network in West Africa per its own materials. Won a 2017 Nelson Mandela-Graca Machel Innovation Award.

name: Nigerian Autistic Society
summary: Abuja-based NGO registered in 1993, one of Nigeria's oldest autism organisations, run by parents, professionals and students, providing education and welfare support and running conferences and training on autism.
notes: STALE/DEAD SITE: nigerianautisticsociety.org and the alternate nigerianautisticsociety.com both fail to resolve (DNS errors) as of September 2026. Existence, history and current centres (Wuse, Apo, Gwagwalada, Utako) confirmed via a third-party autism-awareness directory used here as source_url; could not confirm continued day-to-day activity.

name: Patrick Speech and Languages Centre (PSLC)
summary: Nigeria's first dedicated autism centre, opened in Lagos in 2006, offering speech and language therapy, vocational training, and a professional training academy.
notes: Parent-founded, professionally run; operates two centres in Ikeja and Lekki.

name: She Writes Woman
summary: Lagos-based mental-health advocacy organisation founded by Hauwa Ojeifo in 2016, running a 24-hour toll-free helpline staffed by therapists and counsellors and campaigning on mental-health rights and policy under the mantra 'Nothing about us without us.'
notes: Founder has publicly discussed her own mental-health diagnosis as a motivation; the organisation is not explicitly self-described as survivor-led, so leadership is marked 'mixed' rather than 'nd-led'.

name: The Zeebah Foundation
summary: Abuja nonprofit running The Zeebah Place, a therapy and preparatory-education centre for autistic children, offering ABA, speech and occupational therapy, and life-skills training.
notes: Corporate social responsibility arm of the Levene Energy Group; has served over 100 autistic children. Not stated as autistic-led.

name: auticon Norway
summary: Norwegian branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants, formed after auticon acquired Norwegian IT-testing firm Unicus.
notes: unicus.no now redirects to this page.

name: Autismenyheter
summary: A Norwegian-language news and commentary site about autism, written by a single autistic author from a neurodiversity perspective, covering research and autistic first-person experience.
notes: Run by a single autistic author who publishes under the name 'Soda' and lives on an island near Bergen; launched 3 June 2018 to fill a gap in Norwegian-language autism coverage.

name: Mad in Norway
summary: Norwegian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched in 2019 under editor-in-chief Birgit Valla, publishing critical-psychiatry commentary and research.
region: Oslo (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Editor-in-chief Birgit Valla is a psychologist by training; site does not state the outlet is survivor-led, hence leadership marked unknown rather than assumed.

name: NFU
summary: A Norwegian association for people with intellectual disabilities and their families, based in Oslo, providing legal advice and disability-rights advocacy, with an internal self-advocacy group registered with the European Platform of Self-Advocates.
notes: NFU is a long-running parent-and-self-advocate federation; listed here specifically for its self-advocacy group, an EPSA member. Leadership marked 'mixed' rather than 'nd-led' because the parent body's overall governance was not confirmed to be self-advocate-led on the pages checked.

name: Autism Society of Pakistan (ASP)
summary: National umbrella non-profit registered in 2010, running Autism Resource Centres in Rawalpindi and Islamabad offering diagnosis, therapy, school-integration support, and parent training.
notes: Board of Governors composed of professionals and affected parents. Site returns 403 to a bare curl user agent; resolves 200 with full browser headers.

name: Karachi Down Syndrome Program (KDSP)
summary: Karachi-founded nonprofit, registered in 2014, delivering family support, healthcare, education, and skills programmes for people with Down syndrome, with chapters in four other Pakistani cities.
notes: Registered as a Section 42 nonprofit company; also runs chapters in Faisalabad, Islamabad, Hyderabad, and North Nazimabad.

name: ASO TEA Paraguay
name_local: Asociación de Padres y/o Tutores de Personas con Trastorno del Espectro Autista (ASO TEA)
summary: A Paraguayan parent-and-guardian association for people with autism, active since 2019, that advocates for public policy, runs family support and training, and organizes the annual 'Paraguay Runs for Autism' event.
notes: Parent/guardian-led, not self-advocate-led. Affiliated with the Autism Latin America Federation (ALaFe). President as of 2024-2026: Diana Villalba.

name: Peruvian Autistic People's Association (APEAU)
summary: A Lima-based nonprofit founded in 2023 and composed exclusively of autistic members, advocating for autistic people's rights under the motto 'nada sobre nosotros sin nosotros' and organizing community events in Peru.
notes: The domain asociacionperuanadeautistas.com surfaced in search results but did not resolve on repeated checks; using their active Instagram (posts through late 2025, includes Hispanoamerican Autism Congress participation) as url/source_url instead. Also active on Facebook.

name: Teatro La Plaza
summary: Theatre in Lima, Peru, founded in 2003 by a group of artists including director Chela De Ferrari (non-disabled); internationally known for productions 'Hamlet' (2021) and 'Ricardo III' (2023), which cast actors with Down syndrome.
notes: General theatre venue directed by non-disabled founder; Down-syndrome casting applies to specific acclaimed productions, not a standing disabled ensemble. Site blocks some browser user-agents (403 on one UA, 200 on another) — confirmed live either way.

name: Autism Society Philippines (ASP)
summary: National nonprofit founded in 1989 with about 16,000 members across 106 local chapters, working toward social acceptance and self-reliance for autistic Filipinos.

name: Autism-Poland Coalition
summary: A Warsaw-based coalition of Polish autism organisations doing national advocacy, running an information centre and legal support, and promoting supported-housing 'Home Communities' for autistic adults.
notes: Listed as 'Autism Poland Association' in Autism-Europe's August 2026 member directory; office shares an address with the Synapsis Foundation in Warsaw. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Fundacja ADHD
summary: Polish foundation providing psychological consultations, ADHD and autism diagnostic assessments, crisis support and public education for neurodivergent people nationwide.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations. No single headquarters city stated.

name: Fundacja Autism Team
summary: Łódź-based Polish foundation, founded 2016, combining autistic people, families, experts and therapists to run youth and parent support clubs, crisis intervention, school inclusion programmes and creative 'Artegracja' projects.
notes: Site describes staff as 'osoby w spektrum autyzmu, ich rodziny, eksperci i terapeuci' (autistic people, their families, experts and therapists), hence marked mixed rather than nd-led.

name: Jasna Strona Spektrum
summary: Polish autism information and support website for diagnosed and undiagnosed autistic children and adults, publishing articles on daily life, self-advocacy and diagnosis and running parent workshops.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Leadership not stated on the site; no fixed city given.

name: JiM Foundation
summary: A Łódź-based Polish foundation running diagnostic and therapy clinics and schools for autistic and ADHD children, offering free screening, legal aid, and public campaigns such as 'Quiet Hours'.
notes: Registered in Poland's National Court Register (KRS 0000127075). Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Polish Dyslexia Society (PTD)
summary: Polish learned society on dyslexia running regional branches, an advisory clinic, and courses and training on specific learning difficulties, with an active branch in Gdańsk.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Site is mostly navigation/image-based; national headquarters not clearly stated, so located at its documented Gdańsk branch.

name: Synapsis Foundation
summary: A Warsaw foundation running diagnostic and therapy centres for autistic children and adults, plus Poland's first social enterprise and training home for autistic adults, and training for specialists and parents.
notes: The domain listed for Synapsis in Autism-Europe's official directory (synapsis.waw.pl) is now a dead placeholder page; synapsis.org.pl is the current live site. Site references a 20th-anniversary milestone in 2026 for one of its centres, but the foundation's own founding year is not directly confirmed.

name: APPDA Coimbra
name_local: Associacao Portuguesa para as Perturbacoes do Desenvolvimento e Autismo de Coimbra
summary: A regional Portuguese autism association running a job-insertion social microenterprise (a kiosk inside Coimbra's paediatric hospital since 2018), a laundry training scheme and a university cafe for employing autistic adults.
notes: One of several autonomous regional APPDA associations (Lisboa, Norte/Porto, Coimbra) formed after the original national body split in 2002; included specifically for its employment microenterprise programmes, distinct from any national federation entry.

name: Brainstorm
summary: A Portuguese self-advocacy association founded by and for people with ADHD (PHDA) that runs peer WhatsApp communities and campaigns for a more informed, neuro-inclusive society.
notes: Founded 2024, publicly launched 2025. No confirmed physical headquarters was found; it operates nationally online, so Lisbon is used only as an approximate anchor point.

name: Dislex
summary: A Portuguese association founded by academics and clinicians that researches dyslexia, provides adult self-assessment tools and resources for families, and campaigns for teacher training on dyslexia.
notes: Founded by researchers and clinicians including Vítor da Fonseca; run by a professional board rather than by dyslexic people themselves. Has publicly criticised lack of teacher training for dyslexia support.

name: Mad in Portugal
summary: Portuguese affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism and lived-experience writing in Portuguese.
region: Lisbon (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

name: Ouvir Vozes Movement Portugal
summary: Portugal's national hearing-voices movement, publishing peer information and coping strategies via a WordPress blog, listed as Portugal's Intervoice contact.
notes: Distinct from the editorial site Mad in Portugal, also in this file.

name: Voz do Autista (APVA)
summary: Aveiro-based self-advocacy association of autistic adults, parents and autistic health/education professionals, running an online rights-guidance service, employment support projects and free resources for autistic people.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Describes itself as 'an association of autists, for autists.'

name: Mad in Puerto Rico
summary: Puerto Rican affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism and lived-experience writing in Spanish for a Puerto Rican audience.
region: San Juan (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network; distinct from the older Mad in America Hispanohablante / Mad in (S)pain lineage.

name: Shafallah Center for Persons with Disabilities
summary: Doha center founded in 1999, now under the Qatar Social Work Foundation, providing education, rehabilitation and community-integration services for people with intellectual disabilities and autism under age 21.

name: Help Autism
summary: Romania's largest autism organisation, founded around 2010 and based in Bucharest, running eight therapy centres nationwide, a digital platform for specialists and families, and inclusive camps and sports programmes.
notes: Founded and led by Daniela Bololoi; run by professionals and specialists rather than a self-advocacy model. Listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year inferred from a '16 years' reference on the site as of February 2026.

name: suntAutist
summary: Romanian association publishing 'autism explained by autistics' articles by autistic contributors, opposing ABA and conversion-style therapies and offering resources for autistic children, women and men.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Tagline 'Autismul explicat de autiști' (autism explained by autistics); named autistic contributors write the site's articles. No fixed city stated.

name: Prostor
summary: A Serbian mental-health NGO running peer creative workshops, mental-health campaigns and volunteering programmes with people who use psychiatric services; Serbia's node of the Balkan Voices hearing-voices network.
region: Novi Sad (approximate; exact city not stated on site)
notes: City is an approximation from general knowledge of the organisation, not confirmed on its own about page; a moderator should verify.

name: Union of Serbian Autism Associations
name_local: Savez udruženja Srbije za pomoć osobama sa autizmom
summary: A Belgrade-based union of member associations from across Serbia that raises public awareness of autism and seeks systemic legal and policy solutions for autistic people's rights.
notes: Listed as 'Serbian Society for Autism' in Autism-Europe's August 2026 member directory. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Autism Resource Centre (Singapore)
summary: Singapore charity registered in 2000 providing lifelong services for autistic people, including Pathlight School, early intervention, employment support, and caregiver training.
notes: Runs Pathlight School, Singapore's first autism-focused school.

name: Dyslexia Association of Singapore
summary: Singapore social enterprise and International Dyslexia Association Global Partner providing assessment, specialist tutoring and teacher training for people with dyslexia and other specific learning differences.

name: A Centrum
summary: Slovak organisation running education, conferences and a self-advocacy programme ('Kľúče k sebaobhajobe') on autism, Asperger syndrome and neurodiversity, involving neurodivergent young people as volunteers and advocates.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Leads courses/podcasts through Viera Hincová; not explicitly stated whether the organisation itself is autistic-led.

name: S.P.O.S.A. (Slovak Autism Society)
name_local: Spoločnosť na pomoc osobám s autizmom
summary: A Bratislava-based Slovak national association offering autism education, counselling, a virtual-reality autism simulator, and the 'Autists at Work' employment training programme.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Site footer shows a 2016 copyright year, which may not reflect the organisation's actual founding date; leadership composition not stated.

name: Association of NGOs for Autism Slovenia
summary: A Slovenian national association bringing together NGOs working on autism, listed as an Autism-Europe affiliated member representing the country's autism community.
notes: The site returns an automated bot-verification page to scripted requests, so it could not be read directly; its existence and role are confirmed via Autism-Europe's official August 2026 member directory. Founding year and leadership composition unconfirmed.

name: Mad in Slovenia
summary: Slovenian affiliate of the Mad in the World network, launched in spring 2025, publishing critical-psychiatry articles, professional contributions and a resource page for relatives; grew to over 70 members by December 2025.
region: Ljubljana (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: One of the newest Mad in the World affiliates as of this writing.

name: Autism Somalia Center
name_local: Hay'ada Daryeelka Caruurta Baahiyaha Gaarka Qaba
summary: Founded in 2019 in Garowe, Puntland, the first specialised centre in the region providing assessment, special education, occupational and physiotherapy, and family support for children with autism, Down syndrome and cerebral palsy.
notes: Not in the original country list for this batch but included as a verified, active organisation extending African-continent coverage. Leadership not stated.

name: Autism South Africa
summary: National non-profit providing information, guidance, training, and advocacy for autistic people and their families across South Africa's nine provinces.
notes: Registered Public Benefit Organisation; leadership structure not stated on site.

name: Centre for Autism Research in Africa (CARA)
summary: University of Cape Town interdisciplinary clinical research programme studying autism across the African context, offering African research training fellowships and hosting international conferences.
notes: Based in UCT's Division of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry; set to host the INSAR 2027 annual meeting in Cape Town. Original short URL cara.uct.ac.za redirects here; academically run, not autistic-led.

name: Down Syndrome South Africa (DSSA)
summary: National umbrella body founded in 1986 with 12 regional associations, working to improve quality of life, independence and rights for people with Down syndrome and other intellectual disabilities across South Africa.
notes: Umbrella of 12 regional associations; leadership team structure given but no single named executive.

name: Neurodiversity Foundation
summary: Cape Town foundation founded in 2017 that brings specialists into underserved rural South African communities to identify children with neurodevelopmental differences and trains teachers and community leaders to support them.
notes: Co-founded by a clinical researcher and a counselling psychologist; not stated as neurodivergent-led despite the name.

name: South African Federation for Mental Health (SAFMH)
summary: National mental-health human-rights federation describing a roughly century-long history of advocacy in South Africa, running public education, youth advocacy, and policy and legislation work on mental health.
notes: Site describes 'a 100-year track record of advocacy in South Africa' but does not give an exact founding year; headquarters city inferred from an 011 (Johannesburg) contact number.

name: The Key School
summary: Johannesburg special-needs school founded in 1975, one of the city's oldest, providing specialised autism education addressing cognitive, communication, sensory and social development for children aged 2-12.
notes: Original domain thekeyschool.co.za redirects to thekeyschool.org.

name: Autism Society of Korea
summary: Seoul national association representing autistic people and their families in Korea, working on rights advocacy, welfare policy and social-integration programmes since gaining Ministry recognition in 2006.
notes: Site returns 403 to automated bot checks; live operation confirmed via its active YouTube channel and a public-hospital welfare-directory listing.

name: estas
summary: Self-advocacy group of adult autistic people in South Korea, founded in 2013, campaigning on rights issues such as involuntary tracking devices and diagnostic classification, and taking part in international autism policy forums.
notes: No independent website; organizes and publishes via Facebook. Explicitly independent of welfare centres and parent-led organisations; corroborated by Korean Wikipedia and Ablenews coverage.

name: AMATDAH
name_local: Asociación Madrileña de Adultos con TDAH
summary: A Madrid association run by and for adults diagnosed with ADHD, which grew out of patient meetings at a specialty clinic, offering peer support and pressing institutions on adult ADHD rights.
notes: Grew out of peer meetings among patients at Madrid's Centro de Especialidades Argüelles from 2012. amatdah.org returned HTTP 429 (rate-limited) on repeated automated checks in this session; existence and current activity were confirmed via the SID-INICO and SOM360 directories instead.

name: Asperger Catalunya
name_local: Associacio Espectre Autista - Asperger de Catalunya
summary: A Barcelona-based family association for autistic people, with satellite offices in Viladecans, Granollers, Cornella and Igualada, offering diagnosis support, social-skills groups and leisure activities.
notes: Site describes itself as formed by families with one or more autistic members; no language of autistic self-leadership found.

name: Asperger Madrid
summary: A Madrid association founded in 2003 by parents of children with Asperger syndrome, now staffed by clinical professionals, offering diagnosis, therapy, social-skills groups and employment support.
notes: Board is parent-led with professional clinical staff; ISO 9001 certified. Not to be confused with a similarly named aspergermadrid.org domain.

name: Autismo Diario
summary: A Spanish-language autism information portal, active since 2007, publishing research summaries, education and therapy guidance, and running a free online course platform, edited mainly by Daniel Comin.
notes: No fixed physical headquarters confirmed on-site; located at a generic Spain anchor point since it operates as a national online publication. Domain moved from autismodiario.org (redirects) to autismodiario.com.

name: CEPAMA (Committee for the Promotion and Support of Autistic Girls and Women)
name_local: Comité para la Promoción y Apoyo de las Niñas y Mujeres Autistas
summary: Spanish association of autistic women working on the rights, visibility and research access of autistic girls and women, including a participatory research project with the University of Lisbon on employment, education and healthcare.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site states 'somos mujeres autistas' (we are autistic women) and describes governance by autistic women.

name: Debajo del Sombrero
summary: Debajo del Sombrero is a Madrid nonprofit platform, active since 2007, running an assisted art studio and gallery where professional staff accompany artists with intellectual disabilities in creating, exhibiting, and selling contemporary art.
notes: debajodelsombrero.org (alternate domain) timed out on curl (20s connection timeout) and was not used; debajodelsombrero.es returned 200 OK. 2007 founding date is from third-party arts-press coverage (masdearte.com, mediacionartistica.org) found before search quota ran out, not an explicit dated claim on the official site itself.

name: Fundación CADAH
summary: Spanish online resource and training organisation on ADHD, publishing guidance for families and teachers and running courses on classroom support for children with ADHD.

name: Fundación PRODIS
summary: Madrid foundation providing vocational training and job placement for young people and adults with intellectual disabilities, working with employers on workplace inclusion.

name: Gautena
summary: Basque autism association based in San Sebastián providing diagnosis, schooling and vocational training for autistic people across Gipuzkoa province.

name: Mad Pride Madrid (Orgullo Loco)
summary: A Madrid psychiatric-survivor collective organising around Mad Pride, publishing a blog on mental-health activism, deinstitutionalization and reclaiming madness as identity rather than illness.
notes: Part of the same Latin/Iberian Orgullo Loco movement as the Buenos Aires and Chile entries already in the atlas.

name: Radio Nikosia
summary: A Barcelona association producing a weekly radio programme made entirely by people with psychiatric diagnoses, broadcast on the free station Radio Contrabanda from the Ateneu Enciclopedic Popular in Raval.
notes: radionikosia.org returned HTTP 403 to automated checks in this session (likely bot-blocking); existence and current activity confirmed via SOM360, Coop57's entity registry and the newspaper Diagonal. Registered as Associacio Socio Cultural Radio Nikosia in Barcelona; participants are people in mental-health treatment producing their own media.

name: CSAAT - Sri Lankan Collaborative for Autism Assistive Technology
summary: Research group at SLIIT university in Sri Lanka developing technology-enabled tools and assessments for autism spectrum disorder.
notes: University-affiliated academic/professional group, not a self-advocacy or community organisation.

name: Autism Sverige
summary: Sweden's national autism federation, based in Stockholm and organised into district associations, providing information, an ombudsman service, policy advocacy, and a training centre for professionals and families.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Dyslexiförbundet
summary: Swedish national federation for people with dyslexia and dyscalculia, based in Stockholm, offering educational and workplace guidance, a writing-support helpline, assistive-technology information and a member magazine.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Patron is Prince Carl Philip of Sweden.

name: Inre Ringen Sverige
summary: A nationwide Swedish self-advocacy network within the disability federation FUB for people with intellectual disabilities, publishing the magazine UNIK and holding member assemblies where self-advocates issue policy statements.
notes: Operates as the self-advocate-led wing of the parent-founded federation FUB, present in municipalities across Sweden; Stockholm used as FUB's national base. Member of EPSA.

name: KIND – Center of Neurodevelopmental Disorders at Karolinska Institutet
summary: Karolinska Institutet research and clinical centre in Stockholm studying autism, ADHD and other neurodevelopmental conditions, combining outpatient assessment with academic research programmes.

name: Mad in Sweden
summary: Swedish affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, research summaries and therapy-policy commentary in Swedish.
region: Stockholm (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: Part of the Mad in the World network.

name: Organiserade Autister
summary: Swedish interest association of and for autistic people (formerly known as Organiserade Aspergare), running discussion groups and community activities and promoting neurodiversity and self-determination.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site describes itself as 'an interest association of and for autists.' Likely the current name of the organisation previously known as Organiserade Aspergare; no fixed city stated.

name: Unicus Sweden
summary: Swedish IT-testing consultancy employing autistic consultants, part of a Nordic company model that trains and places autistic professionals with client businesses.
notes: The Norwegian branch (unicus.no) has since become auticon Norway.

name: auticon Switzerland
summary: Swiss branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: Autism Switzerland
summary: A Zurich-based Swiss network organisation providing an autism information platform, a nationwide directory of specialised services by canton, therapeutic training, and public-awareness campaigns.
notes: Full member of Autism-Europe. Operates alongside partner organisations for French- and Italian-speaking Switzerland (including Autisme Suisse Romande). Founding year and leadership composition not stated on the site.

name: Collection de l'Art Brut
summary: The founding art brut museum, opened 1976 in Château de Beaulieu, Lausanne, from Jean Dubuffet's 1971 donation of ~5,000 works to the city; now holds over 60,000 pieces.
notes: Curatorial institution run by the City of Lausanne, not artist-led. Many original works came from psychiatric patients, but the collection deliberately spans self-taught/marginal creators beyond that population.

name: Netzwerk Stimmenhören Schweiz (Swiss Hearing Voices Network)
summary: Switzerland's national Hearing Voices Network, coordinating peer groups and information for voice-hearers and listed as Switzerland's Intervoice contact.

name: Theater HORA
summary: Zurich ensemble theatre founded in 1993 by Michael Elber, part of Stiftung Züriwerk since 2002; all ensemble actors have a certified cognitive/learning disability, while artistic and overall direction is held by non-disabled staff.
notes: 18 full-time ensemble actors are IV-certified with cognitive disability; overall/artistic direction is non-disabled. 'Freie Republik HORA' lab (since 2013) lets ensemble members direct/choreograph their own work.

name: Autism Society of Taiwan
summary: National civic association based in Taipei serving autistic people and families, running vocational and social training as well as diagnostic and employment support.
notes: Runs the 'Star Kids Workshop' vocational and social training programme.

name: FACT - Autism Foundation of the Republic of China
name_local: 中華民國自閉症基金會
summary: Taipei foundation of about 35 years' standing running training courses, group homes and workshops for autistic people, plus free public lectures on autism.
notes: Site references a '35th anniversary' celebration, placing founding around 1990-1991; not independently confirmed.

name: The Association of Parent for Thai Persons with Autism
name_local: สมาคมผู้ปกครองบุคคลออทิซึม (ไทย)
summary: Bangkok-based nonprofit working alongside the Autistic Thai Foundation on quality-of-life programmes for autistic people, including sports, digital learning, and IT skills training.
notes: Parent association; partners with the government-accredited Autistic Thai Foundation.

name: Denizli Autism Association (DOD)
summary: A rights-based Turkish civil-society organisation in Denizli, founded around 2016, publishing reports on discrimination against autistic people, offering family counselling, and sitting on the Turkish Autism Council.
notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member; its General Secretary sits on the Autism-Europe Board of Directors. A regional rather than national body, distinct from the Turkish national anchor organisation Tohum Otizm already in this dataset. Founding year inferred from a '10th anniversary' reference in recent site news.

name: Otizm Vakfi (Autism Foundation)
summary: Ankara foundation established mainly by parents in 2010 to run a life and care centre for autistic children, offering early intervention, education, sports and vocational programmes.
notes: Distinct from the larger Tohum Otizm Vakfi already in the dataset.

name: Tohum Otizm Vakfı (Tohum Autism Foundation)
summary: Istanbul-based public-benefit foundation focused on early diagnosis and special education for autistic children, and on national autism screening and awareness campaigns.

name: Autism Awareness Uganda
summary: Kampala-based community organisation of parents, professionals, and volunteers running caregiver training, awareness campaigns, and referral support for autistic people.

name: Save Children with Autism Uganda (SCAU)
summary: Kampala-based organisation providing childcare support, awareness campaigns, training and a proposed support centre for children with autism, run by director Ismail Jamada.
notes: Site states over 3 years of activity as of its most recent copy, suggesting founding around 2018 or earlier; not precisely stated.

name: Uganda Society for Disabled Children (USDC)
summary: Kampala-headquartered organisation founded in 1985 promoting inclusive healthcare, education and social-inclusion services for Ugandan children and youth with disabilities across 14 core districts.
notes: Broad childhood-disability organisation rather than neurodiversity-exclusive; included for its intellectual-disability and learning-disability work. Not stated as disabled-led.

name: Child With Future
summary: A Kyiv-based Ukrainian foundation, active since around 2011, running a developmental kindergarten and international autism conferences, and representing Ukraine on Autism-Europe's board since 2012.
notes: Autism-Europe affiliated member. Founding year inferred from a '15 years' reference on the site; leadership composition not stated.

name: Dubai Autism Center
summary: UAE nonprofit established by government decree providing assessment, intervention, rehabilitation, and community-awareness programs for autistic children.

name: All Wales People First
summary: The united voice of local self-advocacy groups for people with learning disabilities in Wales, led entirely by people with a learning disability, campaigning nationally and coordinating local groups.
notes: Site states it is 'the only national member-led organisation that represents the voice of people with a learning disability' in Wales.

name: Ambitious about Autism
summary: UK charity running TreeHouse School and Ambitious College for autistic children and young people, alongside campaigning and information services for autistic students and families.
notes: Founded by parents; runs schools and a college rather than solely campaigning.

name: ARGH Scotland
summary: Scottish charitable incorporated organisation based in the Highlands whose committee and full voting members are all autistic, doing collective advocacy, lobbying and campaigning on autism services across Scotland.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. The listed EUCAP URL (arghscotland.co.uk) now redirects permanently to arghscotland.org, used here. Partners with the Scottish Government on autism strategy.

name: Aucademy
summary: A UK community interest company run by autistic educators that trains NHS trusts and professionals from an autistic perspective, publishes educational content, and runs the Kent and Medway autism community of practice.
notes: Registered as Aucademy CIC (Community Interest Company); run by autistic educators including Dr Chloe Farahar and David Gray-Hammond. Operates the NeuroConnect Hub community platform.

name: auticon UK
summary: UK branch of auticon, an IT and business consultancy employing autistic people as consultants and providing neuroinclusion training to client organisations.
notes: Part of the international auticon network.

name: Autism Research Centre, University of Cambridge
summary: University research centre studying the causes and experience of autism across the lifespan, running studies on cognition, biology, and support needs and publishing openly accessible resources.

name: Autistic Mutual Aid Society Edinburgh (AMASE)
summary: Edinburgh-based Autistic People's Organisation whose full members are all autistic, running peer support, an online 'My Autism Story' event series, Autistic Pride and Weird Pride Day gatherings, and policy statements.
notes: Full member of EUCAP. Site states 'all full members are autistic.' Most events run online.

name: Autistic UK
summary: A community interest company run by autistic adults across Wales, England and Scotland that campaigns on policy, publishes position statements, and builds peer networks for autistic people.
notes: Operated as an unincorporated voluntary organisation from 2009, then incorporated as a CIC in 2019 (registered office Caernarfon, Wales, per Companies House).

name: Autistica
summary: UK autism research charity that funds and commissions studies, sets research priorities with autistic people and families, and campaigns for evidence-based support and services.
notes: States it involves autistic people in setting research priorities.

name: Autscape
summary: An annual multi-day conference run by and for autistic people, with workshops, social time and sensory-considered spaces, organised by a UK registered charity.
notes: Registered UK charity since 2011; most organisers are autistic. Venue varies by year, recently High Leigh in Hoddesdon; some years run as an online-only edition.

name: Bethlem Museum of the Mind
summary: Museum of mental health history and patient art on the grounds of Bethlem Royal Hospital (Beckenham), opened in its current Art Deco building in March 2015 as the public face of the Bethlem Art and History Collections Trust (est. 1970).
notes: Run by the hospital-linked charitable trust; archive/collection roots go back to 1970. Distinct from the separate Bethlem Gallery, which is more directly artist-facing.

name: Blue Apple Theatre
summary: Winchester, UK theatre company founded in 2005 by Jane Jessop, producing theatre, dance, singing and film with performers who have learning disabilities; operates as a working name of the Minstead Trust charity.
notes: Founded by Jane Jessop (non-disabled), mother of company member Tommy Jessop, who has Down syndrome; site separates 'Performers' from 'Staff/Facilitators/Trustees'.

name: Bristol University Neurodiversity Society
summary: A student society at the University of Bristol run for and by neurodivergent students, holding weekly drop-ins and credited with helping establish four sensory rooms on campus.
notes: Achieved Gold Bristol SU Accreditation in 2024-25 and 2025-26. Distinct from the Neurodiversity Society at UWE Bristol, a separate institution in the same city.

name: British Dyslexia Association (BDA)
summary: English registered charity providing dyslexia and dyscalculia assessments, teacher training and accreditation, a helpline, and a Dyslexia Friendly Quality Mark for schools and workplaces.
notes: Effective member of the European Dyslexia Association. Registered charity 289243.

name: DaDaFest
summary: Biennial disability and Deaf arts festival in Liverpool produced by DaDa, a self-described disability-controlled/disability-led arts organisation with roots to 1984; the festival launched in 2001.
notes: Parent org DaDa traces roots to 1984 (as Arts Integrated Merseyside/North West Disability Arts Forum); DaDaFest festival itself began 2001.

name: Exceptional Individuals
summary: UK recruitment and workplace-support agency specialising in placing neurodivergent candidates and providing coaching and access-to-work support once they are hired.

name: Flow Observatorium
summary: An equality and diversity charity and creative hub for neurodivergent artists in Portsmouth, running free co-creation sessions and training arts organisations to be neurodivergent-enabling.
notes: Founded with Arts Council England funding, led by neurodivergent artist Jon Adams with Donna Bish. Runs 'KoCreate' sessions with Portsmouth Autism Community Forum. Site is hosted on Wix and may change address.

name: Genius Within
summary: UK community interest company providing coaching, assessment and training for neurodivergent adults in work and job-seeking, and consulting with employers on inclusive practice.
notes: Community interest company; describes services as co-produced drawing on staff lived experience.

name: Hearing Voices Network (England)
summary: A small national charity, run mostly by volunteers, that supports and connects local peer-support groups across England for people who hear voices, see visions or have other unusual perceptions.
notes: Does not run local groups directly, only supports and networks them; work is carried out mostly by volunteers including trustees. Exact founding year not confirmed on-site.

name: Heart n Soul
summary: South East London arts organisation making music and performance work, originating from 1984 creative sessions in Lewisham and formally founded 1987; explicitly led by people with and without learning disabilities and autistic people.
notes: Founding date varies across sources (1984 workshops, 1986 performance company, 1987 per Shape Arts timeline); leadership language ('led by people with and without learning disabilities and autistic people') is the org's own self-description.

name: Hijinx Theatre
summary: Cardiff-based inclusive theatre company founded in 1981 by Gaynor Lougher and Richard Berry; centers learning disabled and/or autistic artists as its core ensemble, currently under co-CEOs Ben Pettitt-Wade and Eloise Tong.
notes: Founders and current leadership are not disclosed as disabled; org's own language centers learning disabled/autistic artists as creative contributors without stating they hold governance roles.

name: Limpsfield Grange School
summary: State day and residential special school in Surrey for autistic girls and girls with communication and interaction needs, known for co-authoring books on autistic girls' experience with its students.

name: Mad in the UK
summary: British affiliate of the Mad in the World network, publishing critical-psychiatry journalism, blogs and 'around the web' roundups since 2018, distinct from the earlier-founded Mad in Ireland.
region: London, England (national scope; editorial base not stated)
notes: About page returned 403 to automated requests; founding confirmed instead via the site's own 2018 welcome post.

name: Mind the Gap
summary: Bradford-based learning disability and autism performance and live-arts company founded in 1988 by Tim Wheeler and Susan Brown; learning disabled and autistic artists co-create productions and help steer the company's creative work.
notes: Site states artists 'directly influence and steer' the work and its vision is a world where 'learning disabled and autistic voices lead the way' — aspirational/future-tense, not a present-tense 'led by' claim. Current joint CEOs show no disability disclosure.

name: National Autistic Taskforce (NAT)
summary: British autistic-run body, founded 2018, that campaigns for better services for autistic people with high support needs, publishing independent care-quality guides and running the EQUALS Project on decision-making support.
notes: Associate member of EUCAP. Describes itself as 'an innovative autistic-run body' focused on autistic people less able to self-advocate. No single headquarters city stated; placed at London as a national placeholder.

name: National Survivor User Network (NSUN)
summary: England's national lived-experience-led mental health charity, connecting and amplifying people with lived experience of mental distress and user-led grassroots groups, based in London.
notes: Self-describes as 'England's only lived experience-led national mental health charity'. Registered address: 483 Green Lanes, London N13 4BS.

name: Neuk Collective
summary: Scotland-wide community and advocacy network for neurodivergent artists, run under Door in the Wall Arts Access CIC (a disabled-led organisation) and founded by neurodivergent textile artist Tzipporah Johnston.
notes: Exact founding year not stated on the site (its own 'Our story'/'history' subpages 404'd during verification); currently active with a directory, membership, and a 2026 Glasgow exhibition.

name: Neurodiversity in Business (NiB)
summary: UK charity and membership network helping employers build neuroinclusive workplaces through research, training and a community of practice for HR and diversity professionals.
notes: Formerly at neurodiversityinbusiness.org, which now redirects here.

name: Oska Bright Film Festival
summary: Biennial film festival in Brighton founded in 2004 by learning-disabled filmmakers, screening only films made by or featuring learning-disabled and/or autistic people, run today by a learning-disabled programming team under Carousel.

name: Participatory Autism Research Collective (PARC)
summary: A voluntary UK network, started at London South Bank University, that brings autistic scholars and activists together with early-career researchers to promote autistic involvement in autism research.
notes: Co-founded by Damian Milton and Nicola Martin; first meeting April 2015. Now spans several UK institutions including Birmingham, Sheffield Hallam and Nottingham. Active in 2026 per site events listing.

name: Raw Vision
summary: Quarterly print and online magazine devoted to outsider art and art brut, founded by John Maizels in London in 1989 and now headquartered in Radlett, Hertfordshire.
notes: Edited/founded by art historian John Maizels, not by neurodivergent or disabled staff explicitly.

name: Recovery in the Bin (RITB)
summary: A UK critical-theorist and activist collective that critiques mainstream 'recovery' models in mental health, publishing survivor-led frameworks like the '#Neorecovery' critique and the Unrecovery Star.
region: United Kingdom (online collective; no fixed city stated)
notes: Site explicitly publishes a piece titled '#Neorecovery: A Survivor Led Conceptualisation and Critique', supporting the nd-led designation.

name: Scottish ADHD Coalition
summary: Scottish charity, founded 2017 out of a 2016 Dundee meeting of local groups, coordinating voluntary organisations across Scotland that support adults and children with ADHD, including youth groups, parent training and referral information.
notes: One of ADHD Europe's newest (2025) national member organisations, though the coalition itself dates to 2017. Registered Scottish charity SC047320.

name: Scottish Autism
summary: Scotland's largest autism-specific service provider, founded in 1968 by a group of parents, running residential and day support, an advice line, family support and participatory research through its Centre for Practice, Policy and Research.
notes: Included as a large, well-known ally-led anchor organisation for Scotland, in contrast to the autistic-led ARGH Scotland and AMASE entries in this batch.

name: Soteria Network UK
summary: A UK network of service users, survivors, carers, activists and professionals promoting the drug-free or minimum-medication Soteria House model for people experiencing psychosis.
region: United Kingdom (online network; no fixed city stated)
notes: Self-describes as part of 'an international movement of service users, survivors, activists, carers, academics and professionals'.

name: Survivor Researcher Network
summary: A UK network for and by psychiatric-survivor and service-user researchers, hosted by the National Survivor User Network (NSUN), supporting peer-led mental-health research and skill-sharing.
notes: Operates as a programme of NSUN, also in this file, rather than as a separately incorporated organisation.

name: The Museum of Everything
summary: UK registered charity and travelling museum for self-taught, art brut and outsider art, founded by James Brett in London in 2009; operates the Gallery of Everything, its commercial space on Chiltern Street.
notes: Site 301-redirects to musevery.com (HTTP 200). Curated by founder James Brett, not by ND/disabled people themselves. Touring model plus fixed Gallery of Everything retail space; recent (2025/26) exhibition dates not independently confirmed.

name: Unlimited
summary: UK commissioning body backing new work by disabled artists since 2012, delivered in partnership by disability-led charity Shape Arts and producer Artsadmin, staging periodic festivals in London.
notes: Originally conceived by Arts Council England for the 2012 Cultural Olympiad; delivery partnership pairs disability-led Shape Arts with Artsadmin, which is not disability-led per available sources — hence 'mixed' rather than 'nd-led'.

name: UWE Bristol Neurodiversity Society
summary: A student-led society at the University of the West of England for autistic, ADHD, dyslexic, dyspraxic and dyscalculic students, running social events, guest speakers and a monthly 'Special Interest Saturday'.
notes: Described on its own page as shaped by its members as well as its elected committee; a separate institution from the University of Bristol's BUNS.

name: Academic Autism Spectrum Partnership in Research and Education
summary: Community-based participatory research partnership, based at Portland State University, in which autistic adults are equal partners with academics. Known for work on healthcare access and other autistic-adult priorities.
notes: Long-standing partner of the Autistic Self Advocacy Network and Autism Society of Oregon; the /about-us/ page returned a 404 during this check, verified instead via the homepage and third-party coverage.

name: AHEADD
summary: US organisation coaching college students with autism, ADHD and learning disabilities on academic, social and career skills, and consulting with universities on support services.

name: Arts of Life
summary: Chicago nonprofit founded in 2000 providing studio space, art supplies, and exhibition and sales support to artists with intellectual and developmental disabilities, with additional studios on Chicago's North Shore.

name: Aspiritech
summary: Illinois nonprofit social enterprise that trains and employs autistic adults as software testers and quality-assurance analysts for outside clients.

name: auticon US
